groups.title: Enteric-Coated Tablet (111001ATE)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to inhibit the formation of blood clots in myocardial infarction, cerebral infarction and unstable angina; to inhibit the formation of blood clots after coronary artery bypass graft surgery (CABG) or percutaneous transluminal coronary angioplasty (PTCA); and to reduce cardiovascular risk in high-risk patients (patients with combined risk factors such as a family history of ischaemic heart disease, high blood pressure, high blood cholesterol, obesity or diabetes).
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 tablet per dose, 1 time in 1 day. Because this is an enteric-coated tablet, it may be taken before a meal with plenty of water.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it or to another salicylate preparation, analgesic, anti-inflammatory medicine or antirheumatic medicine; if you have peptic ulcer; if you have or have had aspirin asthma; if you have haemophilia, severe liver impairment, severe kidney impairment, severe cardiac insufficiency or a tendency to bleed; if you are being given methotrexate at 15 mg or more a week (15 mg/week); or if you are in the third trimester of pregnancy. In the first and second trimesters of pregnancy, do not take this medicine unless it is really necessary.

Before using this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have kidney impairment; impaired cardiovascular circulation (renovascular disease, congestive heart failure, reduced body fluid, major surgery, sepsis or a major bleeding event and the like); liver impairment; impaired heart function; bronchial asthma; if you are about to have surgery; if the user is a young child aged 3 years or younger; if you are an older person; if you have glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency or Reye's syndrome; if the user is 14 years of age or younger with chickenpox or influenza infection; or if you have gout.

Because of the risk of bleeding, tell your doctor that you are taking this medicine if you are having surgery (including dental surgery). Take care not to damage the enteric coating of the tablet.

Do not use it together with other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics or salicylate preparations, or with methotrexate at 15 mg or more a week (15 mg/week), because bleeding may increase or kidney function may decline. Consult a pharmacist if you are taking an anticoagulant, some non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics such as ibuprofen or naproxen, a thrombolytic, another antiplatelet medicine, a haemostatic, a diabetes medicine (insulin preparations, tolbutamide and the like), a uricosuric (benzbromarone, probenecid), a thiazide diuretic, a lithium preparation, a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor, digoxin, a systemically acting adrenocortical hormone preparation (except hydrocortisone used as replacement therapy for Addison's disease), an angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor or a valproic acid preparation. Do not mix it with alkaline preparations (for example sodium bicarbonate, magnesium carbonate) or with preparations that easily absorb moisture. Taken together with alcohol it increases damage to the gastrointestinal mucosa, and the combined effect of this medicine and alcohol may prolong bleeding time.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: signs of shock (for example difficulty breathing, generalised flushing, angioedema, urticaria); an asthma attack; hypersensitivity (erythema, itching, blocked nose, cardiac and respiratory disturbance and, occasionally, rash, swelling, urticaria, rhinitis-like symptoms, conjunctivitis); rarely toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), exfoliative dermatitis, aplastic anaemia, anaemia, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia or reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time); ringing in the ears, deafness, dizziness, headache, excitement, liver impairment; very rarely temporary liver damage, kidney impairment, acute renal failure, hyperventilation, metabolic acidosis, excessive lowering of body temperature, collapse or coldness of the arms and legs. Loss of appetite, heartburn, stomach pain, nausea and vomiting may occur.

summaryTable.What it is for: Inhibition of blood clot formation in myocardial infarction, cerebral infarction and unstable angina, after CABG or PTCA, and reduction of cardiovascular risk in high-risk patients

groups.title: Capsule (101804ACH)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for difficulty in bringing up sputum in acute and chronic bronchitis, bronchial asthma, laryngitis, sinusitis and cystic fibrosis.
groups.usage: For an acute condition, adults: take 1 capsule (200 mg) per dose, 3 times in 1 day; ages 6 to 14 years: take 1 capsule (200 mg) per dose, 2 times in 1 day, before meals with a small amount of water. For a chronic condition, adults: take 1 capsule (200 mg) per dose, 2 times in 1 day; ages 6 to 14 years: take 1/2 capsule (100 mg) per dose, 3 times in 1 day, before meals with a small amount of water. For cystic fibrosis, those aged 6 years and older: take 1 capsule (200 mg) per dose, 3 times in 1 day, before meals with a small amount of water.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, if you have gastric or duodenal ulcer, if the user is a baby under 2 years of age, or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding.

If it is taken together with an oral antibiotic (amoxicillin, cefuroxime, doxycycline, erythromycin, thiamphenicol), leave an interval of at least 2 hours between them.

If, rarely, nausea, vomiting, stomatitis (inflammation inside the mouth), heartburn, diarrhoea, urticaria, itching, rash, headache, tinnitus, bronchospasm (especially in people with asthma), tachycardia or high blood pressure occurs, or, very rarely, anaphylaxis, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Difficulty bringing up sputum in acute and chronic bronchitis, bronchial asthma, laryngitis, sinusitis and cystic fibrosis

groups.title: Oral Solution (A49300ALQ)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used as adjunctive treatment of liver disease.
groups.usage: Adults: take 10 to 30 mL in 1 day, divided into doses taken between meals. Dilute 10 mL of this medicine in about half a cup of water and take it.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have kidney disease, or if you have or have had myocardial infarction.

This medicine cannot be used as an antidote for alcohol poisoning.

If there is no improvement after about 1 month of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. Use this medicine by mouth only; do not use it for injection.

If an adverse reaction occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (130501ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for seasonal and perennial allergic rhinitis, allergic conjunctivitis, chronic idiopathic urticaria and itching of the skin, and, together with a hydrocortisone preparation for external use, for eczema and dermatitis.
groups.usage: Adults and children aged 6 years and older: take 1 tablet (10 mg), 1 time in 1 day, before bedtime. For people who are sensitive to adverse reactions, take 1/2 tablet (5 mg) per dose, divided into a morning and an evening dose, that is 2 doses. The dose may be increased or decreased appropriately according to age and symptoms. In people with kidney impairment the interval between doses must be adjusted according to kidney function, and in children with kidney impairment the dose must be adjusted individually taking account of renal clearance and body weight, so refer to the approved product information for details.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it or to hydroxyzine or piperazine derivatives; if you have renal failure; if the user is a young child under 6 years of age; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are pregnant or breast-feeding; if you have kidney impairment or liver impairment; if you are an older person; if you have epilepsy or a risk of seizures; or if you have a predisposing factor for urinary retention (spinal cord lesion, prostatic hyperplasia and the like).

While you are taking this medicine, do not take it together with theophylline, ritonavir or a large amount of alcohol.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: drowsiness, headache; occasionally malaise, numbness, weakness, agitation, abnormal sensation; rarely mild and temporary lassitude, fatigue, dizziness, a heavy head, excitement, convulsions, dyskinesia, dystonia, fainting, tremor, aggression, confusion, depression, hallucination, insomnia, tic disorder, amnesia, memory disturbance, suicidal ideation, nightmares; occasionally thirst, dry lips, nausea, loss of appetite, stomach discomfort, indigestion, abdominal pain, stomach pain, abdominal discomfort, diarrhoea; rarely vomiting, gastrointestinal disturbance, cheilitis, taste disturbance, increased appetite; rarely rapid heartbeat, arrhythmia, raised blood pressure; occasionally palpitations, vasculitis; occasionally leukopenia, neutropenia, lymphocytosis, eosinophilia; rarely monocytosis, thrombocytosis, thrombocytopenia, photosensitivity; rarely hypersensitivity and anaphylactic shock; occasionally swelling, itching, rash; rarely urticaria, angioneurotic oedema, fixed drug eruption, acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis; rarely blurred vision, conjunctival congestion, disturbance of visual accommodation, oculogyric crisis, vertigo; occasionally liver function disorder with raised AST, ALT, ALP, total bilirubin, gamma-GTP or LDH, jaundice, hepatitis, raised BUN, glycosuria, blood in the urine; rarely difficulty passing urine, bed-wetting, urinary retention, joint pain, muscle pain, pharyngitis, cough, nosebleed, bronchospasm, hearing disturbance, visual disturbance; occasionally chest pain; rarely menstrual disturbance, ringing in the ears, rhinitis or weight gain. After stopping this medicine, itching and urticaria may occur.

summaryTable.What it is for: Seasonal and perennial allergic rhinitis, allergic conjunctivitis, chronic idiopathic urticaria, itching of the skin, and eczema and dermatitis when used with a hydrocortisone preparation for external use

groups.title: Tablet (172806ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for rheumatoid arthritis, juvenile rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis (degenerative joint disease), fever and pain caused by a cold, back pain, dysmenorrhoea, pain after surgery, ankylosing spondylitis, headache, toothache, muscle pain, neuralgia, acute gout, psoriatic arthritis, soft tissue injury (sprain, contusion) and non-articular rheumatic disease (tendinitis, tenosynovitis, bursitis).
groups.usage: For rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, soft tissue injury, non-articular rheumatic disease, acute gout and psoriatic arthritis, adults: take 1/2 tablet to 1.5 tablets (200 to 600 mg) per dose, 3 to 4 times in 1 day; up to 3200 mg may be taken in 1 day. For juvenile rheumatoid arthritis: take 30 to 40 mg per kg of body weight in 1 day, divided into 3 to 4 doses. For mild to moderate pain or a cold, adults: take 1/2 tablet to 1 tablet (200 to 400 mg) per dose, 3 to 4 times in 1 day. Ages 11 to 14 years: 200 to 250 mg per dose; ages 7 to 10 years: 150 to 200 mg per dose; ages 3 to 6 years: 100 to 150 mg per dose; ages 1 to 2 years: 50 to 100 mg per dose, taken by mouth 3 to 4 times in 1 day. In children weighing less than 30 kg the daily amount must not exceed 500 mg, and it is better to avoid taking it on an empty stomach. Do not take more than the recommended dose.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.

Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious and possibly fatal cardiovascular thrombotic events, myocardial infarction and stroke, and serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulceration and perforation may occur.

People with uncontrolled high blood pressure, congestive heart failure, established ischaemic heart disease, peripheral arterial disease or cerebrovascular disease must avoid high-dose ibuprofen (2,400 mg a day); people with cardiovascular risk factors (high blood pressure, high blood lipids, diabetes, smoking and the like) who need high-dose ibuprofen (2,400 mg a day) must consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have or have had gastrointestinal ulcer or gastrointestinal bleeding; if you have a severe blood disorder, severe liver impairment, severe kidney impairment, severe cardiac insufficiency or severe high blood pressure; if you have or have had bronchial asthma; if you have or have had hypersensitivity such as asthma, urticaria or an allergic reaction to aspirin or another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic (including COX-2 inhibitors); if pain occurs before or after coronary artery bypass surgery; if you are in the last 3 months of pregnancy; if you are taking high-dose methotrexate as cancer treatment; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have or have had a blood disorder; if you have a tendency to bleed; if you have liver cirrhosis, or liver impairment now or in the past; if you have kidney impairment now or in the past; if you have cardiac insufficiency or heart disease, high blood pressure, systemic lupus erythematosus or mixed connective tissue disease, ulcerative colitis or Crohn's disease; if you are an older person or the user is a child; if you are pregnant or breast-feeding; or if you have hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 5.

Do not take it together with another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic, low-dose aspirin or high-dose methotrexate. Consult a pharmacist before taking it together with an ACE inhibitor, lithium, furosemide or a thiazide diuretic, a coumarin anticoagulant (warfarin and the like) or a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor.

If an increased risk of myocardial infarction or stroke, or serious and possibly fatal gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulceration or perforation occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: signs of shock (heartburn, chills, difficulty breathing, a fall in blood pressure); blood disorders such as reduced haematocrit, reduced haemoglobin, anaemia, aplastic anaemia, haemolytic anaemia, agranulocytosis, reduced granulocytes, leukocytes or platelets, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time) or eosinophilia; peptic ulcer, gastrointestinal ulcer, gastrointestinal bleeding, perforation, ulcerative colitis, bloody stools, gastritis, pancreatitis, vomiting of blood, Crohn's disease, loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, indigestion, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, upper abdominal pain, thirst, stomatitis, abdominal distension, mouth ulcers, constipation, black stools; Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), photosensitivity reactions, drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS syndrome), angioneurotic oedema, bullous dermatitis, erythema multiforme, maculopapular rash, reddening of the skin, blisters, rash, exfoliative dermatitis, acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis; hepatitis, jaundice, abnormal liver function such as raised GOT, GPT or ALP, liver impairment; hypersensitivity or anaphylactic reactions, an asthma attack, urticaria, eczema, purpura, rash, itching, asthma, bronchoconstriction, difficulty breathing or wheezing; visual disturbance such as blind spots, hearing loss, ringing in the ears, taste disturbance, vertigo, drowsiness, dizziness, depression, headache, a cerebrovascular event or nervousness; aseptic meningitis or meningitis (severe headache, nausea, vomiting, insomnia, a stiff neck, fever or disturbance of consciousness); raised blood pressure, palpitations, heart failure, myocardial infarction or angina; acute renal failure, reduced urine output, blood in the urine, protein in the urine, raised BUN or blood creatinine, high blood potassium, interstitial nephritis, nephrotic syndrome, renal papillary necrosis, reduced urine volume, generalised oedema with breathlessness or lassitude; swelling around the eyes, swelling of the face, malaise, fever, nosebleed, peripheral oedema, or Conn's syndrome of unknown frequency.

groups.title: Soft Capsule (139503ACS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used as adjunctive treatment of eczema and acne, and as adjunctive treatment of disorders of keratinised areas such as fingernails, toenails or hair that split easily.
groups.usage: Take 2 to 4 capsules (1000 to 2000 mg) in 1 day, for 10 to 20 days in 1 month.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have severe kidney dysfunction or hepatic coma, if the user is a child aged 6 years or younger, or if you have cystinuria.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have hypersensitivity to this medicine or if you have kidney stones.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, use it under the supervision of a guardian. If symptoms do not improve after about 1 month of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

If, occasionally, nausea or, rarely, diarrhoea, thirst or mild abdominal pain occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the improvement of acid reflux, heartburn and indigestion caused by reflux of stomach contents (for example after meals, during pregnancy, or when it accompanies reflux oesophagitis).
groups.usage: Adults and children aged 12 years and older: take 10 to 20 mL per dose, 4 times in 1 day (after meals and before bedtime).
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you must strictly limit sodium, as in congestive heart failure or kidney impairment; if you have hypercalcaemia, nephrocalcinosis or recurrent calcium-containing kidney stones; or if the user is a child under 12 years of age.

If symptoms do not improve after 7 days of treatment, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

If it is taken together with tetracycline, digoxin, a fluoroquinolone, an iron salt, ketoconazole, a neuroleptic, thyroxine, penicillamine, a beta blocker (atenolol, metoprolol, propranolol), a glucocorticoid, chloroquine, estramustine or a diphosphonate, leave an interval of at least 2 hours between them.

If an allergic reaction such as itching, bronchoconstriction or an anaphylactic reaction occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.usage: Take 1 tablet per dose: adults (aged 15 years and older) 3 times in 1 day; ages 11 years to under 15 years 2 times in 1 day, before a meal, between meals or after a meal. groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have an acute abdominal disease (appendicitis, intestinal bleeding, ulcerative colitis and the like), if you have intestinal obstruction (blocked bowel), or if the user is a child aged 7 years or younger.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have severe abdominal pain, nausea or vomiting; if you are pregnant or may be pregnant; if you have kidney impairment; or if you have had rectal bleeding or intestinal failure.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, use it under the supervision of a guardian.

Do not take it together with an antacid. Avoid taking it within 1 hour after drinking milk.

If rash or reddening of the skin, itching, severe abdominal pain, diarrhoea, vomiting, abdominal discomfort or cramps occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for contraception and for the treatment of moderate acne in women who can take this medicine.
groups.usage: Take 1 tablet a day for 21 days in the order marked on the pack, then have 7 days without tablets. It is best to take it at about the same time every day. Menstruation occurs during the 7 days without tablets and usually starts 2 to 3 days after the last tablet. If you continue with this medicine, start a new pack of tablets after the 7 days without tablets; menstruation may not have finished before the new pack is started. Refer to the detailed approved product information for further details.
groups.caution:
Because the risk of serious cardiovascular events such as thrombosis may be increased, women taking an oral contraceptive should refrain from smoking. Smokers aged 35 years and older must not take this medicine.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; a tumour (for example breast cancer, endometrial cancer, pituitary tumour); thrombophlebitis, thromboembolism, cerebrovascular or coronary artery disease; undiagnosed abnormal genital bleeding; severe high blood pressure; severe liver impairment; Dubin-Johnson syndrome; Rotor syndrome; jaundice; cholestasis; hepatitis; sickle cell anaemia; severe diabetes; high blood lipids; hyperlipoproteinaemia; porphyria; a metabolic disorder; persistent itching during pregnancy; herpes gestationis; pemphigoid gestationis; otosclerosis; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if you have a pituitary tumour, galactorrhoea or high blood prolactin; if you have migraine with warning signs such as scotoma or fortification spectra; if you have valvular heart disease complicated by pulmonary hypertension or atrial fibrillation; pancreatitis; valvular heart disease with a history of subacute bacterial endocarditis; diabetes with vascular lesions; headache with focal neurological symptoms such as an aura; if you are taking a direct-acting antiviral for hepatitis C; if you have a congenital or acquired hypercoagulable disorder; if you are a smoker aged 35 years and older; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are a smoker; if you have high blood pressure or obesity; if you are a woman aged 40 years and older; if you have epilepsy or migraine; if you have had arterial disease or varicose veins; if you have systemic lupus erythematosus; if you have had breast cancer; if you have or have had depression; if you have heart or kidney failure; if you have atypical hyperplastic breast disease; if you have had breast nodules; if you have valvular heart disease or atrial fibrillation; if you have had high blood lipids; if you have had gallbladder disease or gallstones; if you have endometriosis; if you have asthma or melasma; if you have peripheral circulatory disturbance; if you have diabetes; or if you have migraine without aura.

This medicine does not protect against HIV infection (AIDS) or other sexually transmitted diseases. If you have a severe gastrointestinal disease, absorption may be incomplete, so use an additional method of contraception. This medicine is not for women before their first menstruation or after the menopause. Check the detailed approved product information for full precautions.

Do not take it together with a direct-acting antiviral for hepatitis C (combinations such as ombitasvir, paritaprevir and ritonavir), phenytoin, barbiturates, primidone, carbamazepine, rifampicin, rufinamide, aprepitant, bosentan, efavirenz, oxcarbazepine, topiramate, felbamate, griseofulvin, St John's wort, lipid-lowering medicines or antibiotics. Do not take it with grapefruit juice.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: cardiovascular events (thrombophlebitis, thrombosis and arterial thromboembolism, stroke, cerebral haemorrhage, cerebral thrombosis, myocardial infarction, pulmonary embolism, raised blood pressure, worsening of varicose veins); urogenital symptoms (bleeding between periods, changes in menstrual volume, absence of menstruation and the like); breast symptoms (breast tenderness and enlargement, galactorrhoea, breast pain and the like); digestive symptoms (nausea, vomiting, abdominal distension, liver impairment and the like); central nervous system symptoms (headache, migraine, depression, dizziness and the like); skin symptoms (melasma, acne, erythema multiforme and the like); eye symptoms (visual disturbance, change in corneal refraction and the like); hearing disturbance; metabolic symptoms (sodium and fluid retention and the like); weight change, appetite change, change in libido, speech disturbance, or hypersensitivity reactions (urticaria, angioedema and the like). Check the detailed approved product information for full adverse reactions.

groups.title: Tablet (157301ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for excess stomach acid, heartburn and acid eructation (sour belching).
groups.usage: Those aged 16 years and older: take 1 tablet (10 mg) per dose; up to 2 tablets (20 mg) may be taken in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it or to H2 receptor antagonists, or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have difficulty swallowing food or pain when swallowing, or vomiting of blood or bloody stools; if heartburn has lasted for 3 months or more; if dizziness, drowsiness or cold sweat occurs at the same time; if you have chest or shoulder pain with shortness of breath; if chest pain occurs often; if you have unexpected weight loss, nausea, vomiting or gastrointestinal pain; if you have had hypersensitivity to medicines; if you have kidney impairment, heart disease or liver impairment; if you are an older person; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; or if you are on haemodialysis.

If your body functions change after taking this medicine compared with before, consult a pharmacist. If symptoms do not improve, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist. Do not take this medicine for 14 days or more.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are taking a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic, a medicine for athlete's foot or an antifungal (itraconazole, posaconazole oral suspension and the like), or a tyrosine kinase inhibitor (dasatinib, erlotinib, gefitinib, pazopanib and the like). Consult a pharmacist if you are being given an intravenous lipid preparation. Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: shock, anaphylaxis, difficulty breathing, generalised flushing, swelling of the face, swelling of the throat, urticaria; reduced white blood cells, red blood cells, platelets or eosinophils, anaemia, delayed clotting; Stevens-Johnson syndrome, epidermal necrolysis, rash, urticaria (erythema); abnormal liver function, raised AST (GOT) and ALT (GPT), raised total bilirubin and LDH, jaundice, hepatitis; muscle pain, rhabdomyolysis, joint pain, muscle cramps; slow heartbeat, rapid heartbeat, chest pain, raised blood pressure, facial flushing; ringing in the ears, disturbance of consciousness, convulsions, general lassitude, headache, drowsiness, insomnia, hallucination, agitation, excitement, reduced libido, abnormal sensation, a heavy head, confusion, depression, dizziness; constipation, diarrhoea, thirst, nausea and vomiting, abdominal distension, loss of appetite, stomatitis; interstitial nephritis, acute renal failure, fever, abnormal kidney function test values (raised BUN and creatinine and the like); menstrual disturbance; interstitial pneumonia with high fever, cough, difficulty breathing and abnormal chest X-ray; bronchospasm; breast enlargement in men; or taste disturbance.

groups.title: Tablet (246501ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used as adjunctive treatment of liver disease caused by insufficient bile secretion and of diseases of the biliary system (bile duct, gallbladder), for the improvement of liver function in chronic liver disease, and for indigestion caused by the after-effects of small bowel resection and by inflammatory small bowel disease.
groups.usage: Adults: take 0.5 to 1 tablet (50 to 100 mg) per dose, 3 times in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; severe obstruction of the bile duct; fulminant hepatitis; radio-opaque calcified gallstones; a non-functioning gallbladder; acute cholecystitis; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if the user is a child; if you have kidney disease; if you have peptic ulcer (acute gastric or duodenal ulcer); if you have large or small bowel inflammation such as Crohn's disease; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have severe pancreatic disease, gallstones, variceal bleeding, hepatic coma or ascites, or if you need a liver transplant.

Do not take it together with an oral diabetes medicine (tolbutamide), cholestyramine, colestipol, medicinal charcoal, antacids containing magnesium or aluminium hydroxide, medicines that increase cholesterol secretion from the liver (oral contraceptives containing oestrogen, lipid-lowering medicines such as clofibrate) or medicines that damage the liver.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: occasionally diarrhoea, nausea or vomiting; rarely abdominal pain, constipation, heartburn or stomach discomfort; occasionally itching; rarely rash, fever, cough, difficulty breathing or interstitial pneumonia with abnormal chest X-ray; rarely general lassitude, dizziness, calcification of gallstones, raised liver enzyme values (ALT, ALP, AST, gamma-GT) or reduced white blood cells.

groups.title: Oral Suspension (227730ASS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to remove bubbles in the bowel during gastroscopy, to remove gas in the bowel during abdominal X-ray examination, and to improve abdominal symptoms caused by gas in the gastrointestinal tract (a feeling of fullness in the abdomen, aerophagia and the like).
groups.usage: Adults: to remove bubbles in the bowel for gastroscopy, take 40 to 80 mg with about 10 mL of water 15 to 40 minutes before the examination. To remove gas in the bowel for abdominal X-ray examination, take 40 to 80 mg per dose, 3 times in 1 day, after meals or between meals, starting 3 to 4 days before the examination. To improve abdominal symptoms caused by gas in the gastrointestinal tract, take 40 to 80 mg per dose, 3 times in 1 day, after meals or at bedtime. The dose may be increased or decreased appropriately according to age and symptoms.
groups.caution:
This medicine contains aspartame, which is metabolised in the body to phenylalanine, so it must not be taken by people with phenylketonuria who need to restrict their intake of phenylalanine.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have asthma.

Shake it well before use.

Occasionally loose stools, abdominal discomfort, diarrhoea, abdominal pain, vomiting, nausea, a feeling of heaviness in the abdomen or loss of appetite, and rarely headache or mild irritation of the skin, eyes or mucous membranes may occur.

summaryTable.What it is for: Removal of bubbles or gas in the bowel for gastroscopy and abdominal X-ray, and abdominal symptoms caused by gas in the gastrointestinal tract

groups.title: Tablet (566833ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the supply of selenium in people with selenium deficiency that cannot be made up by nutritional intake.
groups.usage: Take 1 tablet (100 micrograms as selenium), 1 time in 1 day; the dose may be increased to a maximum of 2 tablets (200 micrograms as selenium) in 1 day. Take this medicine with water, without chewing it.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if the user is a baby under 12 months of age; if you have selenium toxicity; or if you have hereditary fructose intolerance, glucose-galactose malabsorption or sucrase-isomaltase deficiency.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have impaired heart or circulatory function, kidney impairment or hypoproteinaemia; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if you have a gastrointestinal disease such as peptic ulcer, chronic ulcerative colitis or regional enteritis; or if the user is a child under 12 years of age.

When it is given to a child, use it under the supervision of a guardian. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.

Do not take it together with a reducing agent such as vitamin C. If you want to take vitamin C, take it separately with an interval of about 4 hours from this medicine. Avoid tannin-containing drinks such as green tea and black tea while taking it and just before and after taking it.

If dermatitis, a bad smell in the sweat or breath, hair loss, irritability, vomiting or allergy occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (254000ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of the various symptoms of a cold, such as runny nose, blocked nose, sneezing, sore throat, cough, chills with shivering, fever, headache, joint pain and muscle pain.
groups.usage: Adults aged 15 years and older: take 1 tablet per dose, 3 times in 1 day, 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome) and toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), have been reported. If a skin rash or any other sign of hypersensitivity appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

If a severe skin adverse reaction such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis occurs, stop taking it and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take this medicine if you have or have had hypersensitivity to it; if you have had asthma after taking this medicine, one of its ingredients, another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine; if the user is a baby under 3 months of age; or if you have severe or uncontrolled high blood pressure.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a child under 2 years of age; if the user is a baby or a child under 15 years of age with, or suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if you have an allergic constitution; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if symptoms of ischaemic colitis such as sudden abdominal pain or rectal bleeding appear in connection with pseudoephedrine; if you have had allergic symptoms caused by a medicine such as fever, rash, joint pain, asthma or itching; if you are an older person, physically weak or have a high fever; or if you are a poor metaboliser of dextromethorphan through CYP2D6.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastric or duodenal ulcer, glaucoma or difficulty passing urine; if you have persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or an ulcer or bleeding problem; or if you smoke or have asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with excessive sputum, a cough lasting or recurring for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough with fever, rash or persistent headache.

If symptoms do not improve after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist. Do not take it continuously for a long period. Drowsiness may occur while taking it; avoid driving a car or operating machinery. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.

While you are taking this medicine, do not take an antitussive-expectorant, another cold medicine, an antipyretic analgesic, a sedative or an oral medicine containing an antihistamine. Do not take this medicine if you are taking an MAO inhibitor used for depression or Parkinson's disease, or have stopped taking one within the past 2 weeks. Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are being given a diabetes medicine, a gout medicine, an arthritis medicine, an anticoagulant or a steroid. Consult a pharmacist if you are being given barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol. Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

If rash and reddening of the skin, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, oedema, difficulty passing urine, persistent or severe thirst, dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, a cerebrovascular event such as stroke, abnormal sensation, myocardial infarction or ischaemic colitis occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

If, rarely, shock (anaphylaxis) occurs with urticaria, swelling and chest tightness soon after taking it, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing, or if Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), asthma, general lassitude, liver function disorder with jaundice, or interstitial pneumonia occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Relief of cold symptoms (runny nose, blocked nose, sneezing, sore throat, cough, chills, fever, headache, joint and muscle pain)

groups.title: Tablet (101305ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for fever and pain caused by a cold, headache, neuralgia, muscle pain, menstrual pain, pain from a sprain, toothache, joint pain and rheumatic pain.
groups.usage: Children aged 12 years and older and adults: take 1 to 2 tablets per dose, 3 to 4 times in 1 day (every 4 to 6 hours) when needed. Take it at the lowest effective dose for the shortest possible period, and do not take more than 8 tablets (4 g) in 1 day.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported. If a skin rash or any other sign of hypersensitivity appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, peptic ulcer, a severe blood disorder, liver impairment, kidney impairment or reduced heart function; if you have or have had aspirin asthma (an asthma attack triggered by a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory medicine); if you have taken barbiturates or tricyclic antidepressants; if you have taken alcohol; or if the user is a child under 12 years of age.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have had hypersensitivity; if you have liver impairment, kidney impairment, peptic ulcer, or a blood disorder now or in the past; if you have a tendency to bleed; if you have impaired heart function; if you have bronchial asthma; if you are an older person; if you are pregnant or breast-feeding; or if your glutathione stores are low.

Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

Consult a pharmacist if you have been given barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol, or if you are taking warfarin or flucloxacillin.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: signs of shock (difficulty breathing, flushing of the whole body, angioedema, urticaria and the like), an asthma attack, thrombocytopenia, granulocytopenia, haemolytic anaemia, methaemoglobinaemia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time), cyanosis, hypersensitivity symptoms (facial swelling, sweating, low blood pressure), nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, gastrointestinal bleeding, peptic ulcer, perforation, rash, allergic reactions, Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), raised AST, raised ALT or fixed drug eruption.

groups.title: Syrup (530800ASY)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the temporary relief of sneezing, runny nose, blocked nose and watering eyes caused by a cold or by allergic and vasomotor rhinitis, and of nasal congestion caused by sinusitis.
groups.usage: Children aged 12 years and older and adults: take 10 mL every 4 hours, and do not exceed 60 mL in 24 hours. Children aged 6 years to under 12 years: take 5 mL every 4 hours, and do not exceed 30 mL in 24 hours. For children aged 2 years to under 6 years, follow the instructions of a doctor.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it or to amine sympathomimetics or antihistamines; if you have an idiosyncratic constitution; if you are breast-feeding; if you have severe high blood pressure, severe coronary artery disease, narrow-angle glaucoma, urinary retention, peptic ulcer, asthma, emphysema or chronic lung disease; or if you are short of breath or have difficulty breathing.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have difficulty breathing such as chronic bronchitis, heart disease, high blood pressure, thyroid disease, diabetes, glaucoma or difficulty passing urine due to prostatic hyperplasia, or if the user is a child.

Take care when driving or operating machinery after taking it.

People taking an MAO inhibitor must not take this medicine. Consult a pharmacist if you take it together with a sedative or a tranquilliser. Avoid alcoholic drinks.

Fear, anxiety, tension, tremor, weakness, pallor, difficulty breathing, difficulty passing urine, insomnia, hallucination, convulsions, central nervous system depression, arrhythmia, dizziness, cardiovascular collapse with low blood pressure, rapid heartbeat, palpitations, headache, nausea, moderate sedation, thirst, weakness, loss of appetite, vomiting, nervousness, excessive urine volume, heartburn, double vision, difficulty passing urine and, rarely, dermatitis, drowsiness or excitement may occur.

groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the improvement of bowel regulation, constipation, loose stools, a feeling of fullness in the abdomen and abnormal fermentation in the intestine caused by disturbance of the intestinal flora (for example by the use of antibiotics or chemotherapeutic agents).
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 capsule (30 mg) per dose, 3 times in 1 day. The dose may be increased or decreased appropriately according to age and symptoms.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have or have had hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 5, or if the user is a baby under 3 months of age.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. If symptoms do not improve after about 1 month of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Consult a pharmacist before using it together with ampicillin, chloramphenicol or cephaloridine.

groups.title: Tablet (347904ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the temporary relief of runny nose, sneezing, itching and watering of the eyes, and itching of the nose or throat caused by pollen allergy or other upper respiratory tract allergy.
groups.usage: Adults and adolescents aged 12 years and older: take 1 tablet per dose with water, at intervals of 12 hours. Do not take more than 2 tablets within 24 hours.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have had hypersensitivity to it.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a child under 12 years of age; if you are an older person aged 65 years and older; if you do not know whether the symptoms are caused by allergic rhinitis, a cold or another cause; if you have been diagnosed with another allergic disease; if nasal congestion is severe; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if you have had allergic symptoms caused by a medicine; if you have kidney impairment; or if you have cardiovascular disease.

Avoid breast-feeding while taking this medicine. Do not exceed the recommended dose.

While you are taking this medicine, do not take a medicine for skin disease, another anti-allergy medicine including an oral medicine for rhinitis, an oral medicine containing an antihistamine, or an antacid containing aluminium or magnesium. Do not take it together with ketoconazole or erythromycin. Do not take it with fruit juices and foods such as grapefruit juice, orange juice or apple juice. Do not drink alcohol before or after taking it.

If dry mouth, constipation, diarrhoea, drowsiness, swelling of the throat, eyelids or lips, rash, itching, urticaria, reddening of the skin, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, indigestion, numbness, headache, fatigue, lassitude, dizziness, insomnia, nervousness, nightmares, sleep disturbance, frequent urination, difficulty passing urine, palpitations, taste disturbance, oedema, chest pain, difficulty breathing, raised blood pressure or menstrual disturbance occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

If, rarely, shock (anaphylaxis) occurs with itching of the skin, urticaria, hoarseness, sneezing, itching of the throat, difficulty breathing, palpitations or clouding of consciousness soon after taking it, or if agranulocytosis, reduced white blood cells or neutropenia occurs with fever, jaundice, brown urine, general lassitude, loss of appetite, sudden high fever, chills or sore throat, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Capsule (153101ACH)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to loosen mucus and help bring up sputum in acute and chronic respiratory disease.
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 capsule (300 mg) per dose by mouth, 2 to 3 times in 1 day. When it is taken for an acute respiratory condition, do not take it continuously for 10 days or more.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, liver cirrhosis, cystathionine synthase deficiency, peptic ulcer, severe kidney impairment or severe liver impairment, or if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have mild or moderate liver impairment; if you have diabetes or are on a low-calorie diet (for the syrup form only); or if you have had hypersensitivity or an allergic reaction to Yellow No. 5.

Consult a pharmacist if you take it together with a cough medicine.

If headache, cold symptoms, difficulty breathing, taste disturbance, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, upper abdominal pain, abdominal pain, heartburn, urticaria, erythema or eczema occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.

Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious and possibly fatal cardiovascular thrombotic events, myocardial infarction and stroke, and serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulceration and perforation may occur.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have had asthma, urticaria or an allergic reaction to aspirin or another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic; if you have gastrointestinal ulcer; if you have bleeding in the gastrointestinal tract, the cerebral blood vessels or elsewhere; if you have a severe blood disorder, severe liver impairment, severe kidney impairment, severe heart failure or severe high blood pressure; if you have bronchial asthma; if pain occurs before or after coronary artery bypass graft surgery (CABG); if you are 6 months or more pregnant; if you are breast-feeding; if you have inflammatory bowel disease such as Crohn's disease or ulcerative colitis; or if you have had gastrointestinal bleeding or perforation.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: rarely shock (difficulty breathing, a fall in blood pressure and the like); blood disorders such as aplastic anaemia, haemolytic anaemia, agranulocytosis, granulocytopenia, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time) or eosinophilia; very rarely thirst, stomatitis, erythema multiforme, systemic lupus erythematosus or hair loss; occasionally angioedema; rarely Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome); drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS syndrome) of unknown frequency; acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, rash, urticaria, itching or purpura; rarely an asthma attack, eczema, an anaphylactic reaction or a photosensitivity reaction; jaundice, raised ALT, raised AST, raised ALP, abnormal liver function or hepatitis; occasionally rhinitis or bronchospasm; rarely a risk of acute pneumonia in people with heart failure; visual disturbance such as loss of vision or scotoma, hearing loss, tinnitus or taste disturbance; fatigue, drowsiness, headache or dizziness; occasionally anxiety, restlessness, confusion or depression; rarely aseptic meningitis, a fall or rise in blood pressure, palpitations, acute renal failure, reduced urine output or blood in the urine, and protein in the urine, raised BUN or blood creatinine, high blood potassium, acute pulmonary oedema, peripheral oedema, fluid retention, reduced fertility in women, swelling around the eye sockets; very rarely malaise, fever, nosebleed or worsening of inflammation.

People with uncontrolled high blood pressure, congestive heart failure, established ischaemic heart disease, peripheral arterial disease or cerebrovascular disease must avoid high-dose ibuprofen (2,400 mg a day); people with cardiovascular risk factors (high blood pressure, high blood lipids, diabetes, smoking and the like) who need high-dose ibuprofen (2,400 mg a day) must consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine.

peptic ulcer, gastrointestinal ulcer, gastrointestinal bleeding, perforation, ulcerative colitis, bloody stools, gastritis, pancreatitis, vomiting of blood, Crohn's disease, loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, indigestion, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, upper abdominal pain, thirst, stomatitis, abdominal distension, mouth ulcers, constipation, black stools; Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), photosensitivity reactions, drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS syndrome), angioneurotic oedema, bullous dermatitis, erythema multiforme, maculopapular rash, reddening of the skin, blisters, rash, exfoliative dermatitis, acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis; groups.title: Soft Capsule (D22200ACS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of the various symptoms of a cold (runny nose, blocked nose, sneezing, sore throat, cough, phlegm, chills with shivering, fever, headache, joint pain, muscle pain).
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and older: take 2 capsules per dose, 3 times in 1 day, 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported. If a skin rash or any other sign of hypersensitivity appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

If a severe skin adverse reaction such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis occurs, stop taking it and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take this medicine if you have or have had hypersensitivity to it; if you have had asthma after taking another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine; if the user is a baby under 3 months of age; or if you are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, anti-Parkinson medicine and the like) or have stopped taking one within the past 2 weeks.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a baby or a child under 15 years of age with, or suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if the user is a baby or young child aged 3 months or older and under 2 years of age; if you have an allergic constitution or have had allergic symptoms (for example fever, rash, joint pain, asthma or itching); if you have liver, kidney, heart or thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastric or duodenal ulcer, glaucoma (for example eye pain or blurred vision) or difficulty passing urine; if you are physically weak or have a high fever; if you have persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or an ulcer or bleeding problem; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; or if you smoke or have asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with excessive sputum, a cough lasting or recurring for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough with fever, rash or persistent headache.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. Do not drink alcohol while taking it. Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery. If symptoms do not improve after 5 to 6 doses, consult a pharmacist.

Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen, an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, anti-Parkinson medicine and the like), an antitussive-expectorant, another cold medicine, an antipyretic analgesic, a sedative, or an oral medicine containing an antihistamine (oral medicine for rhinitis, motion-sickness medicine, anti-allergy medicine). Consult a pharmacist if you have been given barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol. Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

If rash and reddening of the skin, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, oedema, difficulty passing urine, persistent or severe thirst, dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, signs of shock (rarely urticaria, swelling and chest tightness after taking it, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing), Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (high fever with rash and reddening and severe burn-like blisters), acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, a severe skin adverse reaction such as fever, erythema and many small pustules, asthma, general lassitude, jaundice, interstitial pneumonia (cough, breathlessness, difficulty breathing, fever), or symptoms of ischaemic colitis (sudden abdominal pain, rectal bleeding and the like) occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Enteric-coated Tablet (111001ATE)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to inhibit the formation of blood clots in myocardial infarction, cerebral infarction and unstable angina, to inhibit the formation of blood clots after coronary artery bypass graft surgery (CABG) or percutaneous transluminal coronary angioplasty (PTCA), and to reduce cardiovascular risk in high-risk patients (people with combined risk factors such as a family history of ischaemic heart disease, high blood pressure, high blood cholesterol, obesity or diabetes).
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 tablet per dose, 1 time in 1 day. As this is an enteric-coated tablet, it may be taken before meals with plenty of water.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it or to another salicylate preparation; if you have peptic ulcer; if you have or have had aspirin asthma; if you have haemophilia, severe liver impairment, severe kidney impairment, severe cardiac insufficiency or a tendency to bleed; if you are being given methotrexate at a dose of 15 milligrams or more a week (15 mg a week); or if you are in the third trimester of pregnancy.

In the first and second trimesters of pregnancy, do not take this medicine unless it is really necessary.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have kidney impairment; if you have impaired cardiovascular circulation (renal vascular disease, congestive heart failure, reduced body fluid, major surgery, sepsis or a major bleeding event and the like); if you have or have had liver impairment; if you have impaired heart function; if you have or have had a blood disorder; if you have bronchial asthma; if you are about to have surgery; if the user is a young child aged 3 years or younger; if you have hypersensitivity to analgesics, anti-inflammatory medicines or antirheumatic medicines, or an allergic disease; if you are an older person; if you have glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency; if you have Reye's syndrome; if the user is aged 14 years or younger with chickenpox or influenza infection; or if you have gout.

Because there is a risk of bleeding, tell your doctor that you are taking this medicine if you are to have surgery (including dental surgery). Take care not to damage the enteric coating of this medicine.

Do not use it together with a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic or high-dose methotrexate (15 mg a week or more), because bleeding may increase or kidney function may decline when they are given with this medicine.

Consult a pharmacist if you are taking an anticoagulant, a thrombolytic, another platelet aggregation inhibitor, a haemostatic, a diabetes medicine (insulin preparations, tolbutamide and the like), a uricosuric (benzbromarone, probenecid), low-dose methotrexate, a lithium preparation, some non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics such as ibuprofen or naproxen, a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor, digoxin, a systemic corticosteroid (except hydrocortisone used as replacement therapy for Addison's disease), an angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor or a valproic acid preparation. Do not mix it with an alkaline preparation (for example sodium bicarbonate or magnesium carbonate) or with a preparation that easily takes up moisture. When it is taken with alcohol, damage to the gastrointestinal mucosa increases and bleeding time may be prolonged through the combined effect of this medicine and alcohol.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: shock and anaphylactic symptoms (difficulty breathing, generalised flushing, angioedema, urticaria); an asthma attack; hypersensitivity (erythema, itching, blocked nose, cardiac and respiratory disturbance, occasionally rash, swelling, urticaria, rhinitis-like symptoms, conjunctivitis); rarely toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome); drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS syndrome) with fever, rash, lymphadenopathy, facial swelling, hepatitis, nephritis, blood abnormalities, myocarditis or myositis; Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome); exfoliative dermatitis; aplastic anaemia, anaemia, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time); haemolysis and haemolytic anaemia in people with severe glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency; loss of appetite, heartburn, stomach pain, nausea, vomiting; ringing in the ears, hearing loss, dizziness, headache, excitement; rarely liver impairment; very rarely temporary liver damage, kidney impairment, acute renal failure, hyperventilation or metabolic acidosis; Conn's syndrome of unknown frequency (cardiovascular symptoms occurring after an allergy or hypersensitivity reaction associated with coronary artery constriction); an excessive fall in body temperature, collapse or cold limbs.

groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used as an aid in the treatment of osteoporosis, for the prevention of the risk of vitamin D deficiency disease in healthy people without malabsorption, and for the prevention of rickets.
groups.usage: As an aid in the treatment of osteoporosis, adults: take 1 tablet (1000 IU) per dose, 1 time in 1 day. For healthy people without malabsorption and for the prevention of rickets, adults: take 1/2 tablet (500 IU) per dose, 1 time in 1 day. For a young child who has difficulty swallowing the tablet, place the tablet on a spoon, let it disintegrate in water and, if possible, take it with a meal. Take it with plenty of water.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have high blood calcium or high calcium in the urine; if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption; if you have kidney stones; or if the user is a baby under 3 months of age.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a baby under 1 year of age; if the user is a child who gets plenty of sunlight and eats a normal diet; if you have a history of kidney stones; if you have sarcoidosis; if your movement is restricted (a plaster cast); if you have pseudohypoparathyroidism; if you are pregnant or breast-feeding; or if you have kidney impairment.

A young child who has difficulty swallowing this medicine should take the tablet after it has been dissolved in water.

Do not take it together with a benzothiadiazine derivative. Consult a pharmacist if you take it together with another vitamin D preparation, phenytoin or a barbiturate medicine, a thiazide diuretic or a glucocorticoid.

If mental symptoms or disturbance of consciousness (raised blood calcium), headache, nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, weight loss or increased thirst (raised blood calcium), acute symptoms of raised blood calcium (arrhythmia, nausea, vomiting, mental symptoms, disturbance of consciousness), chronic symptoms of raised blood calcium (increased urge to pass urine, increased thirst, loss of appetite, weight loss, kidney stones, calcification of the kidney, calcification in the tissue outside the bone), or muscle and joint pain occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (199501ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis (degenerative joint disease), ankylosing spondylitis, tendinitis, acute gout, dysmenorrhoea, bursitis, skeletal muscle disorders (sprain, contusion, injury, lumbosacral pain), pain after surgery, migraine and pain after tooth extraction.
groups.usage: For rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis and ankylosing spondylitis, adults: take 1 to 2 tablets (275 to 550 mg) per dose, 2 times in 1 day (every 12 hours). For acute gout: take 3 tablets (825 mg) as the first dose, then 1 tablet (275 mg) at intervals of 8 hours until the attack settles. For skeletal muscle disorders, pain after surgery, pain after tooth extraction, dysmenorrhoea, tendinitis and bursitis: take 2 tablets (550 mg) as the first dose, then 1 tablet (275 mg) at intervals of 6 to 8 hours, without exceeding a total of 5 tablets (1375 mg) in 1 day. For migraine: take 3 tablets (825 mg) as the first dose; if needed, 1 to 2 further tablets (275 to 550 mg) may be taken in 1 day, 30 minutes after the first dose. Do not exceed a total of 5 tablets (1375 mg) in 1 day.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.

Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious and possibly fatal cardiovascular thrombotic events, myocardial infarction and stroke, and serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulceration and perforation may occur.

groups.title: Syrup (142334ASY)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to reduce fever caused by an acute upper respiratory tract infection.
groups.usage: Children aged 6 months and older: take 0.4 to 0.6 mL per kg of body weight (5 to 7 mg per kg) per dose at intervals of 4 to 6 hours when needed, without exceeding 4 doses (28 mg per kg) in 1 day. For a child weighing 30 kg or less, do not exceed 25 mL (300 mg) in 1 day. If the body weight is known, dosing by body weight is more appropriate; refer to the approved product information for the recommended dose for each age group.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.

Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious and possibly fatal cardiovascular thrombotic events, myocardial infarction and stroke, and serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulceration and perforation may occur.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, peptic ulcer, a severe blood disorder, severe liver impairment, severe kidney impairment, severe cardiac insufficiency or severe high blood pressure; if you have or have had bronchial asthma; if you have had asthma, urticaria or an allergic reaction to aspirin or another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic (including COX-2 inhibitors); if it is for the treatment of pain occurring before or after coronary artery bypass graft surgery (CABG); or if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding.

Considering the importance of the treatment, either stop breast-feeding or stop taking the medicine. Dizziness or fatigue may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery. When it is taken for a long period for an acute illness, as a rule this should be within 5 days.

Do not take it together with another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic, aspirin or high-dose methotrexate. The dose may be increased or decreased appropriately according to age and symptoms. In people with kidney impairment the dosing interval must be adjusted to kidney function, and in children with kidney impairment the dose must be adjusted individually according to renal clearance and body weight, so refer to the approved product information for details.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it or to hydroxyzine or piperazine derivatives; if you have renal failure; if the user is a young child under 6 years of age; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are pregnant or breast-feeding; if you have kidney impairment or liver impairment; if you are an older person; if you have epilepsy or a risk of seizures; or if you have a predisposing factor for urinary retention (spinal cord lesion, prostatic hyperplasia and the like).

While you are taking this medicine, do not take it together with theophylline, ritonavir or a large amount of alcohol.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: drowsiness, headache; occasionally lassitude, numbness, weakness, agitation or abnormal sensation; rarely mild and temporary listlessness, fatigue, dizziness, a heavy head, excitement, convulsions, movement disorder, dystonia, fainting, tremor, aggression, confusion, depression, hallucination, insomnia, tic disorder, loss of memory, memory disturbance, suicidal ideation or nightmares; occasionally thirst, dry lips, nausea, loss of appetite, stomach discomfort, indigestion, abdominal pain, stomach pain, abdominal discomfort or diarrhoea; rarely vomiting, gastrointestinal disturbance, inflammation of the lips, taste disturbance or increased appetite; rarely rapid heartbeat, arrhythmia or raised blood pressure; occasionally palpitations or vasculitis; occasionally reduced white blood cells, reduced neutrophils, increased lymphocytes or increased eosinophils; rarely increased monocytes, increased or reduced platelets, or photosensitivity; rarely hypersensitivity and anaphylactic shock; occasionally swelling, itching or rash; rarely urticaria, angioneurotic oedema, fixed drug eruption or acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis; rarely blurred vision, conjunctival congestion, disturbance of eye accommodation, oculogyric crisis or vertigo; occasionally liver function disturbance such as raised AST, ALT, ALP, total bilirubin, gamma-GTP or LDH, jaundice, hepatitis, raised BUN, sugar in the urine or blood in the urine; rarely difficulty passing urine, bed-wetting or urinary retention; joint pain, muscle pain, pharyngitis, cough, nosebleed, bronchospasm, hearing disturbance or visual disturbance; occasionally chest pain; rarely menstrual disturbance, ringing in the ears, rhinitis or weight gain.

groups.title: Syrup (172804ASY)

A child weighing less than 30 kg must not be given more than 500 mg in 1 day, and it is better to avoid taking it on an empty stomach. Ages 11 to 14 years: take 200 to 250 mg (10 to 13 mL) per dose. Ages 7 to 10 years: take 150 to 200 mg (8 to 10 mL) per dose. Ages 3 to 6 years: take 100 to 150 mg (5 to 8 mL) per dose. Ages 1 to 2 years: take 50 to 100 mg (3 to 5 mL) per dose. groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.

Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious and possibly fatal cardiovascular thrombotic events, myocardial infarction and stroke, and serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulceration and perforation may occur.

People with uncontrolled high blood pressure, congestive heart failure, established ischaemic heart disease, peripheral arterial disease or cerebrovascular disease must avoid high-dose ibuprofen (2,400 mg a day); people with cardiovascular risk factors (high blood pressure, high blood lipids, diabetes, smoking and the like) who need high-dose ibuprofen (2,400 mg a day) must consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine.

groups.title: Capsule (D94200ACH)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of the various symptoms of a cold (runny nose, blocked nose, sneezing, sore throat, cough, phlegm, chills with shivering, fever, headache, joint pain, muscle pain).
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and older: take 2 capsules per dose. Ages 8 years to under 15 years: take 1 capsule per dose. Take it 3 times in 1 day, 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported. If a skin rash or any other sign of hypersensitivity appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

If a severe skin adverse reaction such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis occurs, stop taking it and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have had asthma after taking another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine; if the user is a baby under 3 months of age or a child under 2 years of age; if you are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, anti-Parkinson medicine and the like) or have stopped taking one within the past 2 weeks; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a baby or a child under 15 years of age with, or suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if you have an allergic constitution or have had allergic symptoms caused by a medicine (for example fever, rash, joint pain, asthma or itching); if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastric or duodenal ulcer, glaucoma (for example eye pain or blurred vision) or difficulty passing urine; if you are an older person, physically weak or have a high fever; if you have persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or an ulcer or bleeding problem; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; or if you smoke or have asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with excessive sputum, a cough lasting or recurring for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough with fever, rash or persistent headache.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, use it under the supervision of a guardian. Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery. If symptoms do not improve after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take it together with an antitussive-expectorant, another cold medicine, an antipyretic analgesic, a sedative, or an oral medicine containing an antihistamine (oral medicine for rhinitis, motion-sickness medicine, anti-allergy medicine). Consult a pharmacist if you take it together with a diabetes medicine, a gout medicine, an arthritis medicine, an anticoagulant, a steroid, barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol. Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

If rash and reddening of the skin, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, oedema, difficulty passing urine, persistent or severe thirst, dizziness, anxiety, tremor or insomnia occurs, or if, rarely, signs of shock (urticaria, swelling and chest tightness soon after taking it, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing), Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (high fever with rash and reddening and severe burn-like blisters), asthma, general lassitude, jaundice or interstitial pneumonia (cough, breathlessness, difficulty breathing, fever) occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

If nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, constipation, low blood pressure, facial flushing, an irregular heartbeat or skin rash occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (A06600ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for constipation and for the relief of the loss of appetite, abdominal distension, abnormal fermentation in the intestine and haemorrhoids that follow constipation.
groups.usage: Adults aged 15 years and older: take 1 tablet per dose, 3 times in 1 day, before meals. For the first dose take the smallest amount, then increase or decrease it gradually while watching the form and condition of the stool.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have an acute abdominal disease such as appendicitis, intestinal bleeding or ulcerative colitis, or if you have intestinal obstruction.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are pregnant or may be pregnant; if you have severe abdominal pain, nausea or vomiting; if you have kidney impairment; or if you have had rectal bleeding or intestinal failure.

If constipation does not improve after about 1 week of use, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist. Do not keep taking it for 1 week or more. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.

Do not take this medicine within 1 hour after taking an antacid or drinking milk. (Avoid drinking milk or taking an antacid within 1 hour after taking this medicine.)

If rash, reddening of the skin, itching, severe abdominal pain, diarrhoea, vomiting, abdominal discomfort or cramps occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.
