groups.title: Tablet (D14400ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of the various symptoms of a cold (sore throat, cough, phlegm, chills with shivering, fever, headache, joint pain, muscle pain).
groups.usage: Take 1 tablet per dose, 3 times in 1 day, 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported. If a skin rash or any other sign of hypersensitivity appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

Do not take this medicine if you have or have had hypersensitivity to it; if you have had asthma after taking another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine; if the user is a baby under 3 months of age; or if you are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, anti-Parkinson medicine and the like) or have stopped taking one within the past 2 weeks.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a baby or a child under 15 years of age with, or suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if the user is a baby or young child under 2 years of age; if you have an allergic constitution or have had allergic symptoms (for example fever, rash, joint pain, asthma or itching); if you have liver, kidney, heart or thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure or gastric or duodenal ulcer; if you are an older person, physically weak or have a high fever; if you have persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or an ulcer or bleeding problem; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; or if you have hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 5 (Sunset Yellow FCF) or Yellow No. 4 (tartrazine).

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. Do not give it to a child under 2 years of age; if it is really necessary, see a doctor. If symptoms do not improve after about 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen, an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, anti-Parkinson medicine and the like), an antitussive-expectorant, another cold medicine, an antipyretic analgesic, a sedative, or an oral medicine containing an antihistamine (oral medicine for rhinitis, motion-sickness medicine, anti-allergy medicine). Consult a pharmacist if you have been given barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol, or if you are being given another medicine such as a diabetes medicine, a gout medicine, an arthritis medicine, an anticoagulant or a steroid. Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

If rash and reddening of the skin, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, high anion gap metabolic acidosis (HAGMA), signs of shock (urticaria, swelling and chest tightness soon after taking it, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing), Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome, with high fever, rash and reddening, and severe symptoms such as burn-like blisters), asthma, general lassitude, jaundice (yellowing of the skin or the whites of the eyes) or interstitial pneumonia (cough, breathlessness, difficulty breathing, fever) occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (162601ATB)

groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have pernicious anaemia or megaloblastic anaemia caused by vitamin B12 deficiency; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have pernicious anaemia, or if you have or have had hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 4.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, use it under the supervision of a guardian.

Consult a pharmacist if you are taking aminosalicylic acid, an oral contraceptive, a dihydrofolate reductase inhibitor (methotrexate, trimethoprim and the like), a hydantoin antiepileptic such as phenytoin, sulfasalazine or cholestyramine.

If allergic symptoms such as erythema, skin rash, itching, general lassitude or difficulty breathing, an anaphylactic reaction, loss of appetite, nausea and vomiting, oedema, weight loss, gastrointestinal disturbance, or central nervous system disturbance such as changes in sleep, poor concentration, hyperactivity, irritability, excitement, depression, confusion or impaired judgement occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (347904ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the temporary relief of runny nose, sneezing, itching and watering of the eyes, and itching of the nose or throat caused by pollen allergy or other upper respiratory tract allergy.
groups.usage: Adults and adolescents aged 12 years and older: take 1 tablet per dose with water, at intervals of 12 hours. Do not take more than 2 tablets within 24 hours.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a child under 12 years of age; if you have kidney impairment; if you are an older person; if you do not know whether the symptoms are caused by allergic rhinitis, a cold or another cause; if you have been diagnosed with another allergic disease such as bronchial asthma or atopic dermatitis; if nasal congestion is severe; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if you have had an allergy caused by a medicine; if you have kidney impairment; or if you have cardiovascular disease.

If you are breast-feeding and take this medicine, do not breast-feed.

Do not take it together with another anti-allergy medicine (medicine for skin disease, oral medicine for rhinitis and the like), an oral medicine containing an antihistamine (cold medicine, antitussive-expectorant, motion-sickness medicine, hypnotic sedative and the like), an antacid (preparations containing aluminium or magnesium), ketoconazole or erythromycin. Do not take it with fruit juices (grapefruit juice, orange juice, apple juice) or with food. Do not drink alcohol before or after taking it.

If dry mouth, constipation, diarrhoea, drowsiness, swelling of the throat, eyelids or lips, rash, itching, urticaria, reddening of the skin, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, indigestion, numbness, headache, fatigue, lassitude, dizziness, insomnia, nervousness, nightmares, sleep disturbance, frequent urination, difficulty passing urine, palpitations, taste disturbance, oedema, chest pain, difficulty breathing, raised blood pressure or menstrual disturbance occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

If agranulocytosis, reduced white blood cells or neutropenia occurs with sudden high fever, chills or sore throat, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

If signs of shock (hypersensitivity symptoms such as difficulty breathing, a fall in blood pressure, angioedema, chest pain or flushing), liver function disturbance (raised AST, ALT, gamma-GTP, ALP or LDH, jaundice and the like), dizziness or nausea occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to loosen mucus and help bring up sputum in acute and chronic respiratory disease.
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 capsule (300 mg) per dose, 2 to 3 times in 1 day. When it is taken for an acute respiratory condition, do not take it continuously for 10 days or more.
groups.caution:
This medicine is not for people with hypersensitivity to it, liver cirrhosis, cystathionine synthase deficiency, peptic ulcer or severe kidney impairment (creatinine clearance below 25 mL/min).

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have mild or moderate liver impairment; if you have had hypersensitivity or an allergic reaction to Yellow No. 203 or Quinoline Yellow WS; or if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding.

Consult a pharmacist if you are taking a cough medicine.

Headache, cold symptoms, difficulty breathing, taste disturbance, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, upper abdominal pain, abdominal pain, heartburn, urticaria, erythema or eczema may occur.

groups.title: Tablet (A04700ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of heartburn associated with excess stomach acid and a burning sensation in the stomach.
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and older: take 1 tablet per dose. Do not take more than 2 tablets within 24 hours.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption; if you have difficulty taking it; or if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a child under 15 years of age; if you have unexplained weight loss or persistent abdominal pain; if you have kidney disease; or if you are on haemodialysis.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. If symptoms do not improve after about 2 weeks of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take it together with another stomach medicine. Consult a pharmacist if you take it together with atenolol, metoprolol, propranolol, chloroquine, a tetracycline antibiotic, diflunisal, digoxin, a diphosphonate, fexofenadine, iron (salts), a fluoroquinolone antibiotic, sodium fluoride, a glucocorticoid, indometacin, ketoconazole, lansoprazole, a phenothiazine antiepileptic, penicillamine, a phosphate, thyroxine, a salicylate or an antacid.

Occasionally nausea, diarrhoea or headache, and rarely anaphylaxis, enzyme abnormalities, constipation, loss of appetite, abdominal discomfort, flatulence (abdominal distension), vomiting, thirst, rash, itching, urticaria, peeling of the skin, fatigue, jaundice, hepatitis, angioneurotic oedema, joint pain or muscle cramps may occur.

groups.title: Tablet (D33500ATB)

Do not take it together with another antipyretic analgesic, a cold medicine or a sedative.

If rash, reddening of the skin, nausea, vomiting, constipation, loss of appetite or vertigo occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (257100ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for paroxysmal pain of gastrointestinal disease and for functional disturbance and spasmodic pain of the biliary system, the urinary system and the female reproductive system, including dysmenorrhoea.
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 to 2 tablets per dose, 3 times in 1 day. Do not exceed a maximum of 6 tablets in 1 day.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Do not take this medicine if you have had hypersensitivity to it (rash, red spots, itching, swelling of the throat, eyelids or lips); if you have had asthma caused by another cold medicine or antipyretic analgesic; if you have severe kidney impairment or glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency; if you have glaucoma; if you have difficulty passing urine due to prostatic hyperplasia; if you have functional narrowing of the gastrointestinal tract such as pyloric stenosis; if you have paralytic or obstructive intestinal obstruction; if you have severe muscle weakness or megacolon; if you have rapid heartbeat or tachyarrhythmia; if you have severe liver impairment, severe heart disease, haemorrhagic colitis, peptic ulcer or a severe blood disorder; or if you have taken barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have bacterial diarrhoea; if you have or have had liver impairment; if you have Gilbert's syndrome (Meulengracht's disease); if you have impaired heart function (coronary insufficiency, heart failure, arrhythmia and the like); if you have or have had kidney impairment; if you have had peptic ulcer; if you have or have had a blood disorder; if you have a tendency to bleed; if you have bronchial asthma, ulcerative colitis, an overactive thyroid or fever; if you have prostatic hyperplasia; if you are an older person; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if you are at risk of narrow-angle glaucoma; if you are prone to obstruction of the bowel or of the outlet of the ureter; or if you are prone to tachyarrhythmia.

Disturbance of eye accommodation may occur, so take care when driving or operating machinery.

People who have taken other products containing acetaminophen, barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol must not take this medicine. Consult a pharmacist if you take it together with warfarin, lithium, a thiazide diuretic, a tetracyclic antidepressant, an antihistamine, an antipsychotic, quinidine, amantadine, disopyramide or another anticholinergic medicine (tiotropium, ipratropium, atropine-like compounds), an antidopaminergic medicine such as metoclopramide, a beta agonist, propantheline, chloramphenicol, probenecid, zidovudine, flucloxacillin or cholestyramine.

If thrombocytopenia, agranulocytosis, cyanosis, leukopenia, granulocytopenia, haemolytic anaemia, methaemoglobinaemia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time), flushing, skin reactions, abnormal sweating, itching, dry skin, urticaria, red spots, a fall in blood pressure including shock, anaphylactic shock, drug eruption, difficulty breathing, hypersensitivity, angioedema, rash, swelling (of the throat, eyelids, lips and the like), chest tightness, cold hands and feet, cold sweat, breathlessness, burn-like blisters, allergic reactions, Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), palpitations, rapid heartbeat, vertigo, fatigue, bronchospasm, thirst, diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, high anion gap metabolic acidosis, abdominal distension, raised transaminases, difficulty passing urine, urinary retention, dilated pupils, ciliary muscle paralysis, disturbance of accommodation (in people with severe long-sightedness), anxiety, excitement, hallucination, headache, a heavy head or abnormally high body temperature occurs, or if unexpected abdominal pain continues or worsens, or occurs with fever, nausea, vomiting, a change in bowel movement, abdominal tenderness, a fall in blood pressure, fainting or bloody stools, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (106301ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for acute and chronic bronchitis and asthmatic bronchitis caused by disturbance of mucus secretion.
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 tablet (30 mg) per dose, 3 times in 1 day. When treatment is continued, take 1 tablet (30 mg) per dose, 2 times in 1 day. This medicine may be taken with or without food.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, severe kidney impairment or severe liver impairment, or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have kidney impairment or peptic ulcer, if you are pregnant or breast-feeding, or if you are an older person.

Consult a pharmacist if you take it together with an antibiotic such as erythromycin, cefalexin, oxytetracycline, amoxicillin, cefuroxime or doxycycline.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: rarely serious skin damage such as Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome) or toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome); fever, itching, rhinitis, and non-specific influenza-like prodromal symptoms such as cough and sore throat; commonly nausea; uncommonly vomiting, diarrhoea, indigestion, abdominal pain, heartburn, dry mouth, stomach discomfort, a feeling of fullness in the stomach or abdomen, constipation or loss of appetite; urticaria, skin rash, an anaphylactic reaction (including anaphylactic shock), urticarial erythema, angioedema, itching or other hypersensitivity reactions, swelling of the face, difficulty breathing, a rise in body temperature with chills; purulent rhinitis with a raised white blood cell count; abnormal sensation of the tongue, a change in taste, numbness in the mouth or a feeling of numbness in the arm.

groups.title: Enteric-coated Tablet (111001ATE)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to inhibit the formation of blood clots in myocardial infarction, cerebral infarction and unstable angina, to inhibit the formation of blood clots after coronary artery bypass graft surgery (CABG) or percutaneous transluminal coronary angioplasty (PTCA), and to reduce cardiovascular risk in high-risk patients (people with combined risk factors such as a family history of ischaemic heart disease, high blood pressure, high blood cholesterol, obesity or diabetes).
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 tablet per dose, 1 time in 1 day. As this is an enteric-coated tablet, it may be taken before meals with plenty of water.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it or to another salicylate preparation, an analgesic, an anti-inflammatory medicine or an antirheumatic medicine; if you have peptic ulcer; if you have or have had aspirin asthma; if you have haemophilia, severe liver impairment, severe kidney impairment, severe cardiac insufficiency or a tendency to bleed; if you are being given methotrexate at a dose of 15 milligrams or more a week (15 mg a week); or if you are in the third trimester of pregnancy. In the first and second trimesters of pregnancy, do not take this medicine unless it is really necessary.

Before using this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have kidney impairment; if you have impaired cardiovascular circulation (renal vascular disease, congestive heart failure, reduced body fluid, major surgery, sepsis or a major bleeding event and the like); if you have liver impairment or impaired heart function; if you have bronchial asthma; if you are about to have surgery; if the user is a young child aged 3 years or younger; if you are an older person; if you have glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency; if you have Reye's syndrome; if the user is aged 14 years or younger with chickenpox or influenza infection; or if you have gout.

Because there is a risk of bleeding, tell your doctor that you are taking this medicine if you are to have surgery (including dental surgery). Take care not to damage the enteric coating of this medicine.

Do not use it together with another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic or salicylate preparation, or with methotrexate at a dose of 15 milligrams or more a week (15 mg a week), because bleeding may increase or kidney function may decline when they are given with this medicine.

Consult a pharmacist if you are taking an anticoagulant, some non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics such as ibuprofen or naproxen, a thrombolytic, another platelet aggregation inhibitor, a haemostatic, a diabetes medicine (insulin preparations, tolbutamide and the like), a uricosuric (benzbromarone, probenecid), a thiazide diuretic, a lithium preparation, a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor, digoxin, a systemic corticosteroid (except hydrocortisone used as replacement therapy for Addison's disease), an angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor or a valproic acid preparation. Do not mix it with an alkaline preparation (for example sodium bicarbonate or magnesium carbonate) or with a preparation that easily takes up moisture. When it is taken with alcohol, damage to the gastrointestinal mucosa increases and bleeding time may be prolonged through the combined effect of this medicine and alcohol.

If signs of shock (for example difficulty breathing, generalised flushing, angioedema, urticaria), an asthma attack, hypersensitivity (erythema, itching, blocked nose, cardiac and respiratory disturbance, occasionally rash, swelling, urticaria, rhinitis-like symptoms, conjunctivitis), rarely toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS syndrome), Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), exfoliative dermatitis, aplastic anaemia, anaemia, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time), loss of appetite, heartburn, stomach pain, nausea, vomiting, ringing in the ears, hearing loss, dizziness, headache, excitement, liver impairment, or very rarely temporary liver damage, kidney impairment, acute renal failure, hyperventilation, metabolic acidosis, an excessive fall in body temperature, collapse or cold limbs occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Oral Solution (130502ALQ)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for seasonal and perennial allergic rhinitis, allergic conjunctivitis, chronic idiopathic urticaria (of unknown cause) and itching of the skin.
groups.usage: Adults and children aged 12 years and older: take 10 mg, 1 time in 1 day. Children aged 2 years to under 12 years: take 10 mg in 1 day if the body weight is 30 kg or more, and 5 mg in 1 day if the body weight is less than 30 kg. For people sensitive to adverse reactions, take it in divided doses in the morning and in the evening. The dose may be increased or decreased appropriately according to age and symptoms. For the recommended dose in people with kidney impairment, refer to the approved product information.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have or have had hypersensitivity to it; if you have or have had hypersensitivity to hydroxyzine or piperazine derivatives; if you have renal failure; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if the user is a baby under 2 years of age; or if you have the rare hereditary defect of fructose intolerance.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have kidney impairment or liver impairment; if you have epilepsy or a risk of seizures; if you are an older person; or if you have a predisposing factor for urinary retention (spinal cord lesion, prostatic hyperplasia).

Do not take it together with theophylline or ritonavir. Do not breast-feed while taking this medicine. Do not take it together with alcohol.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: nervous system effects (drowsiness, headache; occasionally lassitude, numbness, weakness, agitation, abnormal sensation; rarely mild and temporary listlessness, tiredness, dizziness, a heavy head, excitement, convulsions, movement disorder, dystonia, fainting, tremor, aggression, confusion, depression, hallucination, insomnia, tic disorder, loss of memory, memory disturbance, suicidal ideation, nightmares); digestive effects (occasionally thirst, dry lips, nausea, loss of appetite, stomach discomfort, indigestion, abdominal pain, stomach pain, abdominal discomfort, diarrhoea; rarely vomiting, gastrointestinal disturbance, inflammation of the lips, taste disturbance, increased appetite); circulatory effects (rarely rapid heartbeat, arrhythmia, raised blood pressure; occasionally palpitations); blood effects (vasculitis; occasionally reduced white blood cells, reduced neutrophils, increased lymphocytes, increased eosinophils; rarely increased monocytes, increased platelets, reduced platelets); immune system and skin and subcutaneous tissue effects (photosensitivity; rarely hypersensitivity and anaphylactic shock; occasionally swelling, itching, rash; rarely urticaria, angioneurotic oedema, fixed drug eruption, acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis); eye effects (rarely blurred vision, conjunctival congestion, disturbance of eye accommodation, back-and-forth eye movement); ear and labyrinth effects (vertigo); liver effects (occasionally liver function disturbance such as raised AST, ALT, ALP, total bilirubin, gamma-GTP or LDH, jaundice, hepatitis); kidney effects (occasionally raised BUN, sugar in the urine, blood in the urine; rarely difficulty passing urine, bed-wetting, urinary retention); musculoskeletal and connective tissue effects (joint pain); pharyngitis, cough, nosebleed, bronchospasm, hearing disturbance, visual disturbance; occasionally chest pain; rarely menstrual disturbance, ringing in the ears, rhinitis or weight gain.

groups.title: Powder (384300APD)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for pain relief in headache, toothache, pain after tooth extraction, sore throat, earache, joint pain, neuralgia, back pain, muscle pain, shoulder pain, bruise pain, fracture pain, sprain pain, menstrual pain (period pain) and pain from injury, and for reducing fever with chills.

groups.usage: For an acute condition, take 1 capsule (200 mg) per dose: adults 3 times in 1 day, and ages 6 to 14 years 2 times in 1 day, before meals with a small amount of water. For a chronic condition, adults: take 1 capsule (200 mg) per dose, 2 times in 1 day; ages 6 to 14 years: take 1/2 capsule (100 mg) per dose, 3 times in 1 day, before meals with a small amount of water. For cystic fibrosis, ages 6 years and older: take 1 capsule (200 mg) per dose, 3 times in 1 day, before meals with a small amount of water.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have gastric or duodenal ulcer; if the user is a baby under 2 years of age; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding, or if you have had hypersensitivity or an allergic reaction to Yellow No. 5.

If you take it together with an oral antibiotic (amoxicillin, cefuroxime, doxycycline, erythromycin, thiamphenicol), leave an interval of at least 2 hours between them.

If, rarely, nausea, vomiting, stomatitis, heartburn, diarrhoea, urticaria, itching, rash, headache, ringing in the ears, bronchospasm (especially in people with asthma), rapid heartbeat or high blood pressure occurs, or very rarely anaphylaxis occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (142301ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for chronic polyarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, arthrosis, ankylosing spondylitis, painful swelling or inflammation after injury and surgery, and as an aid in the treatment of infections accompanied by inflammation, pain and fever.
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 tablet (300 mg) per dose, 2 to 4 times in 1 day. Do not exceed 4 tablets (1200 mg) in 1 day.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.

Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious and possibly fatal cardiovascular thrombotic events, myocardial infarction and stroke, and serious cardiovascular adverse reactions may occur.

Taking this medicine may cause serious and possibly fatal gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as bleeding, ulceration and perforation of the gastrointestinal tract.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have or have had gastrointestinal ulcer; if you have bleeding in the gastrointestinal tract, the cerebral blood vessels or elsewhere; if you have a severe blood disorder, severe liver impairment, severe kidney impairment, severe heart failure or severe high blood pressure; if you have or have had bronchial asthma; if you have had asthma, urticaria or an allergic reaction to aspirin or another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic; if it is for the treatment of pain occurring before or after coronary artery bypass graft surgery (CABG); if you are 6 months or more pregnant; if you have inflammatory bowel disease such as Crohn's disease or ulcerative colitis; or if you have had gastrointestinal bleeding or perforation during treatment with a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have or have had a blood disorder; if you have a tendency to bleed; if you have or have had liver impairment or kidney impairment; if you have fluid retention or heart failure; if you have high blood pressure; if you have had hypersensitivity; if you have systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) or mixed connective tissue disease (MCTD); if you are an older person; if the user is a child aged 6 years or older; if you have stomach cancer or alcoholism; if you are in early or mid pregnancy or may be pregnant; if you have ischaemic heart disease, peripheral arterial disease, cerebrovascular disease or risk factors for cardiovascular disease (for example high blood pressure, high blood lipids, diabetes, smoking); if you have hepatic porphyria; if you have had major surgery with blood loss; if you are being given a diuretic or an ACE inhibitor; if you have a blood clotting disorder or are being given an anticoagulant; or if you have had hypersensitivity or an allergic reaction to Yellow No. 5.

Considering the importance of the treatment, either stop breast-feeding or stop taking the medicine. Dizziness or fatigue may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery. When it is taken for a long period for an acute illness, as a rule this should be within 5 days.

Do not take it together with aspirin, another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic or high-dose methotrexate. Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you take it together with a corticosteroid, alcohol, digoxin, phenytoin, probenecid, sulfinpyrazone, a sulfonylurea, an ACE inhibitor or angiotensin II receptor antagonist, a diuretic, lithium, a coumarin anticoagulant (warfarin and the like), baclofen, an immunosuppressant (ciclosporin, tacrolimus, sirolimus), a thrombolytic, ticlopidine, an antithrombotic, a medicine that raises blood potassium (for example a potassium-sparing diuretic, an ACE inhibitor, an angiotensin II receptor antagonist, an immunosuppressant such as ciclosporin or tacrolimus, trimethoprim or heparin), an inducer of CYP2C8 or CYP2C9 (for example rifampicin or phenobarbital), low-dose methotrexate (less than 15 mg a week), an antiplatelet medicine, a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor or low-dose aspirin.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: rarely shock (chest discomfort, chills, difficulty breathing, a fall in blood pressure and the like); rarely blood disorders such as aplastic anaemia, haemolytic anaemia, granulocytopenia, leukopenia, agranulocytosis, pancytopenia, thrombocytopenia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time) or eosinophilia; indigestion, abdominal distension, heartburn, upper abdominal pain, diarrhoea or constipation; occasionally loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain or stomach discomfort; rarely oesophagitis, oesophageal stricture, worsening of diverticula, non-specific haemorrhagic colitis, ulcerative colitis or Crohn's disease, peptic ulcer, gastrointestinal bleeding, perforation, bloody stools, gastritis or pancreatitis; very rarely thirst, stomatitis, erythema multiforme, systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) or hair loss; occasionally angioedema; rarely Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome); drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS syndrome) of unknown frequency; occasionally rash, urticaria, itching or purpura; rarely triggering of an asthma attack, eczema, an anaphylactic reaction or a photosensitivity reaction; rarely jaundice, raised ALT, raised AST, raised ALP, abnormal liver function or hepatitis; occasionally rhinitis, bronchospasm or acute pneumonia; rarely visual disturbance such as scotoma or dark spots, hearing loss, tinnitus or taste disturbance; fatigue, drowsiness, headache or dizziness; occasionally anxiety, restlessness, confusion or depression; rarely aseptic meningitis, severe headache, nausea, vomiting, insomnia, a stiff neck, fever or disturbance of consciousness; rarely mental disturbance, agitation, excitement, disorientation or reversible toxic amblyopia; rarely a fall or rise in blood pressure, palpitations, reduced urine output, blood in the urine, protein in the urine, raised BUN or blood creatinine, high blood potassium, reduced urine volume, generalised oedema with breathlessness or lassitude; rarely renal papillary necrosis, nephrotic syndrome, interstitial nephritis, peripheral oedema, acute pulmonary oedema, fluid retention, high blood pressure or heart failure; Conn's syndrome of unknown frequency; reduced fertility in women; occasionally swelling around the eye sockets; very rarely malaise, fever, nosebleed or worsening of inflammation.

groups.title: Capsule (153101ACH)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to loosen mucus and help bring up sputum in acute and chronic respiratory disease.
groups.usage: Adults: take 300 mg per dose by mouth, 2 to 3 times in 1 day. When it is given for an acute respiratory condition, do not take it continuously for 10 days or more.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, liver cirrhosis, cystathionine synthase deficiency, peptic ulcer, severe kidney impairment or severe liver impairment.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have mild or moderate liver impairment; if you have diabetes or are on a low-calorie diet (for the syrup form only); if you have had hypersensitivity or an allergic reaction to Yellow No. 5; or if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding.

Do not take it together with a cough medicine.

If headache, cold symptoms, difficulty breathing, taste disturbance, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, upper abdominal pain, abdominal pain, heartburn, urticaria, erythema or eczema occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (106301ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for acute and chronic bronchitis and asthmatic bronchitis caused by disturbance of mucus secretion.
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 tablet (30 mg) per dose, 3 times in 1 day, with or without food. When treatment is continued, take 1 tablet (30 mg) per dose, 2 times in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, severe kidney impairment or liver impairment, or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have kidney impairment or peptic ulcer, if you are pregnant or breast-feeding, or if you are an older person.

Consult a pharmacist if you take it together with an antibiotic such as erythromycin, cefalexin, oxytetracycline, amoxicillin, cefuroxime or doxycycline.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: serious skin damage such as Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome) or toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome); fever, itching, rhinitis, and non-specific influenza-like prodromal symptoms such as cough and sore throat; commonly nausea; uncommonly mild upper gastrointestinal adverse reactions including vomiting, diarrhoea, indigestion, abdominal pain, heartburn and dry mouth; rarely stomach discomfort, a feeling of fullness in the stomach or abdomen, constipation, loss of appetite, urticaria, skin rash, an anaphylactic reaction (including anaphylactic shock), urticarial erythema, angioedema, itching or other hypersensitivity reactions, swelling of the face, difficulty breathing, a rise in body temperature with chills, purulent rhinitis with a raised white blood cell count, numbness in the mouth or a feeling of numbness in the arm; uncommonly abnormal sensation of the tongue or a change in taste.

groups.title: Tablet (D12500ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of the various symptoms of a cold (sore throat, cough, phlegm, chills with shivering, fever, headache, joint pain, muscle pain).
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and older: take 1 tablet per dose, 3 times in 1 day, 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported. If a skin rash or any other sign of hypersensitivity appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

Do not take this medicine if you have or have had hypersensitivity to it; if you have had asthma after taking another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine; if the user is a child under 2 years of age; if you are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, anti-Parkinson medicine and the like) or have stopped taking one within the past 2 weeks; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a baby or a child under 15 years of age with, or suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if you have an allergic constitution or have had allergic symptoms caused by a medicine (for example fever, rash, joint pain, asthma or itching); if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure or gastric or duodenal ulcer; if you are an older person, physically weak or have a high fever; if you have persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or an ulcer or bleeding problem; or if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. If symptoms do not improve after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take it together with an antitussive-expectorant, another cold medicine, an antipyretic analgesic, a sedative, or an oral medicine containing an antihistamine (oral medicine for rhinitis, motion-sickness medicine, anti-allergy medicine). Consult a pharmacist if you take it together with barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants, alcohol, a diabetes medicine, a gout medicine, an arthritis medicine, an anticoagulant or a steroid. Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

If rash and reddening of the skin, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, oedema, dizziness, anxiety, tremor or insomnia occurs, or if, rarely, signs of shock (urticaria, swelling and chest tightness soon after taking it, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing), Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), general lassitude, jaundice (yellowing of the skin or the whites of the eyes) or interstitial pneumonia (cough, breathlessness, difficulty breathing, fever) occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

If a pregnant woman takes 5,000 IU or more of vitamin A in 1 day, it may cause birth defects. Women within the first 3 months of pregnancy and women who may be pregnant must not take it.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have or have had hypersensitivity to soybean oil; if you have hypersensitivity to soybean or peanut; or if the user is a baby under 3 months of age.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a baby under 1 year of age; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if the user is a premature baby or a young child; if you have or have had hypersensitivity to Red No. 40; if you have a disorder of fat metabolism such as hyperlipoproteinaemia, diabetic hyperlipidaemia or pancreatitis; if lipid emulsions must be given to you with caution; or if you have fat overload.

If symptoms do not improve after about 1 month of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist. The vitamin A in this medicine is supplied sufficiently by a normal diet, so the supplementary dose must not exceed 5,000 IU in 1 day. Children should take it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian. It may turn the urine yellow and so affect clinical test values. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.

If nausea, vomiting, itching, dry and rough skin, painful swelling of the joints, loose stools, diarrhoea, constipation, loss of appetite, red spots, urticaria, eczema, rash, maculopapular rash, itching, or oedema or fluid retention in people with kidney failure or heart failure occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Soft Capsule (172802ACS)

groups.usage: Adults: for rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, soft tissue injury, non-articular rheumatic disease, acute gout and psoriatic arthritis, take 1 to 3 capsules (200 to 600 mg) per dose, 3 to 4 times in 1 day, up to 16 capsules (3200 mg) in 1 day. For juvenile rheumatoid arthritis, take 30 to 40 mg per kg of body weight in 1 day, divided into 3 to 4 doses. For mild to moderate pain or a cold, adults: take 1 to 2 capsules (200 to 400 mg) per dose, 3 to 4 times in 1 day. For migraine, adults: take 1 to 2 capsules (200 to 400 mg) per dose, without exceeding 2 capsules within 24 hours. Adolescents aged 12 years and older: take 1 to 2 capsules (200 to 400 mg) per dose, 3 to 4 times in 1 day. If the body weight is less than 30 kg, the amount in 1 day must not exceed 500 mg, and it is better to avoid taking it on an empty stomach.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.

Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious and possibly fatal cardiovascular thrombotic events, myocardial infarction and stroke, and serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulceration and perforation may occur.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have or have had gastrointestinal ulcer or gastrointestinal bleeding; if you have a severe blood disorder, severe liver impairment, severe kidney impairment, severe cardiac insufficiency or severe high blood pressure; if you have or have had bronchial asthma; if you have or have had hypersensitivity such as asthma, urticaria or an allergic reaction to aspirin or another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic; if pain occurs before or after coronary artery bypass surgery; or if you are in the last 3 months of pregnancy.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have had hypersensitivity; if you have or have had a blood disorder; if you have a tendency to bleed; if you have liver cirrhosis, or liver impairment now or in the past; if you have kidney impairment now or in the past; if you have cardiac insufficiency or heart disease or high blood pressure; if you have systemic lupus erythematosus or mixed connective tissue disease; if you have ulcerative colitis or Crohn's disease; if you are an older person or the user is a child; or if you are pregnant or breast-feeding.

Do not take more than the recommended dose. When it is taken for a cold, as a rule this should be within 5 days; without the instruction of a doctor or pharmacist, do not take it for pain for 10 days or more (adults) or 5 days or more (children), and do not take it for fever for 3 days or more.

Do not take it together with high-dose methotrexate or another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic. Consult a pharmacist if you take it together with low-dose aspirin, an ACE inhibitor, lithium, furosemide or a thiazide diuretic, low-dose methotrexate, a coumarin anticoagulant (warfarin and the like) or a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: signs of shock (chest discomfort, chills, difficulty breathing, a fall in blood pressure and the like); blood disorders such as reduced haematocrit or haemoglobin, anaemia, aplastic anaemia, haemolytic anaemia, agranulocytosis, granulocytopenia, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time) or eosinophilia; peptic ulcer, gastrointestinal ulcer, gastrointestinal bleeding, perforation, ulcerative colitis, bloody stools, gastritis, pancreatitis, vomiting of blood, Crohn's disease, loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, indigestion, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, upper abdominal pain, thirst, stomatitis, abdominal distension, mouth ulcers, constipation, black stools; Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), photosensitivity reactions of unknown frequency, drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS syndrome) of unknown frequency, angioneurotic oedema, bullous dermatitis, erythema multiforme, maculopapular rash, reddening of the skin, blisters, rash, exfoliative dermatitis, acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis; hepatitis, jaundice, abnormal liver function such as raised GOT, GPT or alkaline phosphatase (ALP), liver impairment; hypersensitivity or anaphylactic reactions, an asthma attack, urticaria, eczema, purple spots, itching, asthma, bronchoconstriction, difficulty breathing or wheezing; visual disturbance such as scotoma, hearing loss, ringing in the ears, taste disturbance, vertigo, drowsiness, dizziness, depression, headache, a cerebrovascular event or nervousness; aseptic meningitis or meningitis; a fall or rise in blood pressure, palpitations, heart failure, myocardial infarction or angina; acute renal failure, reduced urine output, blood in the urine, protein in the urine, raised BUN or blood creatinine, high blood potassium, interstitial nephritis, nephrotic syndrome, renal papillary necrosis, reduced urine volume, generalised oedema with breathlessness or lassitude; swelling around the eyes, swelling of the face, malaise, fever, nosebleed, oedema or peripheral oedema.

If symptoms do not improve after taking it for 1 week, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. Unless it is really necessary, children aged 10 years or younger should avoid taking it.

Do not take this medicine within 1 hour after an antacid or after drinking milk.

If rash and reddening of the skin, itching, severe abdominal pain, diarrhoea, vomiting, abdominal discomfort or cramps occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have severe pancreatic disease or gallstones.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.

Do not take it together with an oral diabetes medicine (tolbutamide), cholestyramine, colestipol, medicinal charcoal, antacids containing magnesium or aluminium hydroxide, medicines that reduce cholesterol in the bile (for example oral contraceptives containing oestrogen), medicines that reduce cholesterol in the blood (for example clofibrate), or medicines that damage the liver.

groups.title: Syrup (142334ASY)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to reduce fever caused by an acute upper respiratory tract infection.
groups.usage: Children aged 6 months and older: take 0.4 to 0.6 mL per kg of body weight (5 to 7 mg per kg) per dose at intervals of 4 to 6 hours when needed, without exceeding 4 doses (28 mg per kg) in 1 day. For a child weighing 30 kg or less, do not exceed 25 mL (300 mg) in 1 day. If the body weight is known, dosing by body weight is more appropriate; refer to the approved product information for the recommended dose for each age group.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.

Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious and possibly fatal cardiovascular thrombotic events, myocardial infarction and stroke, and serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulceration and perforation may occur.

This medicine contains aspartame, which is metabolised in the body to phenylalanine, so it must not be taken by people with phenylketonuria who need to restrict their intake of phenylalanine.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, peptic ulcer, a severe blood disorder, liver impairment, kidney impairment, heart failure or high blood pressure; if you have or have had bronchial asthma; if you have had asthma, urticaria or an allergy caused by aspirin or another anti-inflammatory analgesic; if it is for the treatment of pain before or after coronary artery bypass surgery; or if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have or have had peptic ulcer, a blood disorder, a tendency to bleed, liver impairment or kidney impairment; if you have heart failure or high blood pressure; if you have a history of hypersensitivity; if you have systemic lupus erythematosus or mixed connective tissue disease; if you have ulcerative colitis or Crohn's disease; if you are an older person or the user is a child; if you have stomach cancer; if you take low-dose aspirin to prevent myocardial infarction or stroke; or if the user is a baby under 6 months of age.

When it is taken for a long period, as a rule this should be within 5 days.

Do not use it together with another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic, aspirin or high-dose methotrexate. Consult a pharmacist if you use it together with a glucocorticoid, alcohol, digoxin, phenytoin, probenecid, sulfinpyrazone, a sulfonylurea, a diuretic with an antihypertensive, an ACE inhibitor, furosemide, lithium, low-dose methotrexate or a coumarin anticoagulant (warfarin and the like).

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: rarely signs of shock (chest discomfort, chills, difficulty breathing, a fall in blood pressure); aplastic anaemia, haemolytic anaemia, granulocytopenia, thrombocytopenia, reduced platelet function or eosinophilia; peptic ulcer, gastrointestinal bleeding, perforation, ulcerative colitis, bloody stools, gastritis, pancreatitis; Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome) or Lyell's syndrome (toxic epidermal necrolysis); drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS syndrome) of unknown frequency; jaundice, raised GOT, GPT or AL-P; triggering of an asthma attack, urticaria, eczema, purpura; loss of vision or scotoma; aseptic meningitis (severe headache, nausea, vomiting, insomnia, a stiff neck, fever or disturbance of consciousness); reduced urine output, blood in the urine, protein in the urine, raised BUN or blood creatinine, high blood potassium; occasionally rash or itching.

Reduced urine volume, generalised oedema with breathlessness or lassitude, acute pulmonary oedema, occasionally loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, indigestion, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort or swelling around the eye sockets, rarely hearing loss, ringing in the ears, taste disturbance, a fall or rise in blood pressure or palpitations, and very rarely thirst, stomatitis, abdominal distension, constipation, malaise, fever or nosebleed may occur.

groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and older: take 2 capsules per dose, 3 times in 1 day, 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported. If a skin rash or any other sign of hypersensitivity appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

If a severe skin adverse reaction such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis occurs, stop taking it and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take this medicine if you have or have had hypersensitivity to it; if you have had asthma after taking another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine; if the user is a baby under 3 months of age; or if you have severe or uncontrolled high blood pressure.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a baby or a child under 15 years of age with, or suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if the user is a baby or young child under 2 years of age; if you have a constitution prone to allergy or have had allergic symptoms (for example fever, rash, joint pain, asthma or itching); if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastric or duodenal ulcer, glaucoma (for example eye pain or blurred vision) or difficulty passing urine; if you are an older person, physically weak or have a high fever; if you have persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or an ulcer or bleeding problem; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; or if you smoke or have asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with excessive sputum, a cough lasting or recurring for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough with fever, rash or persistent headache.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. Do not take it continuously for a long period. Drowsiness may occur after taking this medicine, so take care when driving or operating machinery. If symptoms do not improve after about 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen, an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, anti-Parkinson medicine and the like), an antitussive-expectorant, another cold medicine, an antipyretic analgesic, a sedative, or an oral medicine containing an antihistamine (oral medicine for rhinitis, motion-sickness medicine, anti-allergy medicine). Do not take this medicine if you have stopped taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, anti-Parkinson medicine and the like) within the past 2 weeks. Consult a pharmacist if you have been given barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol, or another medicine such as a diabetes medicine, a gout medicine, an arthritis medicine, an anticoagulant or a steroid. Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

If rash and reddening of the skin, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, oedema, difficulty passing urine, persistent or severe thirst, dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, signs of shock (rarely urticaria, swelling and chest tightness after taking it, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing), Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (with high fever, rash and reddening of the skin and severe burn-like blisters), acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, a severe skin adverse reaction such as fever, erythema and many small pustules, asthma, general lassitude, jaundice, interstitial pneumonia (cough, breathlessness, difficulty breathing, fever) or symptoms of ischaemic colitis (sudden abdominal pain, rectal bleeding and the like) occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

If symptoms of posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome or reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome (sudden severe headache, thunderclap headache, nausea, vomiting, confusion, seizure, visual disturbance and the like) occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Soft Capsule (142301ACS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for chronic polyarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, arthrosis, ankylosing spondylitis, painful swelling or inflammation after injury and surgery, and as an aid in the treatment of infections accompanied by inflammation, pain and fever.
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 capsule (300 mg) per dose, 2 to 4 times in 1 day. Do not exceed 4 capsules (1200 mg) in 1 day.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.

Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious and possibly fatal cardiovascular thrombotic events, myocardial infarction and stroke, and serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulceration and perforation may occur.

People with uncontrolled high blood pressure, congestive heart failure, established ischaemic heart disease, peripheral arterial disease or cerebrovascular disease must avoid high-dose dexibuprofen (1,200 mg a day); people with cardiovascular risk factors (high blood pressure, high blood lipids, diabetes, smoking and the like) who need high-dose dexibuprofen (1,200 mg a day) must consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have or have had gastrointestinal ulcer; if you have bleeding in the gastrointestinal tract, the cerebral blood vessels or elsewhere; if you have a severe blood disorder, severe liver impairment, severe kidney impairment, severe cardiac insufficiency or severe high blood pressure; if you have or have had bronchial asthma; if you have had asthma, urticaria or an allergic reaction to aspirin or another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic; if it is for the treatment of pain before or after coronary artery bypass graft surgery (CABG); if you are 6 months or more pregnant; if you are breast-feeding; if you have inflammatory bowel disease such as Crohn's disease or ulcerative colitis; or if you have had gastrointestinal bleeding or perforation during earlier treatment with a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have or have had a blood disorder; if you have a tendency to bleed; if you have or have had liver impairment or kidney impairment; if you have fluid retention or heart failure; if you have high blood pressure; if you have had hypersensitivity; if you have systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) or mixed connective tissue disease (MCTD); if you are an older person; if the user is a child aged 6 years or older; if you have stomach cancer or alcoholism; if you are in early or mid pregnancy or may be pregnant; if you have ischaemic heart disease, peripheral arterial disease, cerebrovascular disease or risk factors for cardiovascular disease (for example high blood pressure, high blood lipids, diabetes, smoking); if you have hepatic porphyria; if you have had major surgery with blood loss; if you have a blood clotting disorder or are being given an anticoagulant; or if you have or have had hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 5 (Sunset Yellow FCF).

Considering the importance of the treatment, either stop breast-feeding or stop taking the medicine. Dizziness or fatigue may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery. When it is taken for a long period for an acute illness, as a rule this should be within 5 days.

Do not take it together with aspirin, another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic or high-dose methotrexate (15 mg a week or more) used as cancer treatment. Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you take it together with a corticosteroid, alcohol, digoxin, phenytoin, probenecid, sulfinpyrazone, a sulfonylurea, an ACE inhibitor, an angiotensin II receptor antagonist, a diuretic, lithium, a coumarin anticoagulant (warfarin and the like), baclofen, an immunosuppressant (ciclosporin, tacrolimus, sirolimus), a thrombolytic, ticlopidine, an antithrombotic, a medicine that raises blood potassium (trimethoprim, heparin and the like), an inducer of CYP2C8 or CYP2C9 (for example rifampicin or phenobarbital), low-dose methotrexate (less than 15 mg a week), an antiplatelet medicine or a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor, or if you take low-dose aspirin to prevent myocardial infarction or stroke.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: rarely shock (chest discomfort, chills, difficulty breathing, a fall in blood pressure and the like); rarely blood disorders such as aplastic anaemia, haemolytic anaemia, granulocytopenia, leukopenia, agranulocytosis, pancytopenia, thrombocytopenia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time) or eosinophilia; indigestion, abdominal distension, heartburn, upper abdominal pain, diarrhoea or constipation; occasionally loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain or stomach discomfort; rarely oesophagitis, oesophageal stricture, worsening of diverticula, non-specific haemorrhagic colitis, ulcerative colitis or Crohn's disease, peptic ulcer, gastrointestinal bleeding, perforation, bloody stools, gastritis or pancreatitis; very rarely thirst, stomatitis, erythema multiforme, systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) or hair loss; occasionally angioedema; rarely Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome); drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS syndrome) of unknown frequency; acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis; occasionally rash, urticaria, itching or purpura; rarely triggering of an asthma attack, eczema, an anaphylactic reaction or a photosensitivity reaction; rarely jaundice, raised ALT, raised AST, raised ALP, abnormal liver function or hepatitis; occasionally rhinitis, bronchospasm or acute pneumonia; rarely visual disturbance such as scotoma or dark spots, hearing loss, tinnitus or taste disturbance; fatigue, drowsiness, headache or dizziness; occasionally anxiety, restlessness, confusion or depression; rarely aseptic meningitis, severe headache, nausea, vomiting, insomnia, a stiff neck, fever or disturbance of consciousness; rarely mental disturbance, agitation, excitement, disorientation or reversible toxic amblyopia; rarely a fall or rise in blood pressure, palpitations, reduced urine output, blood in the urine, protein in the urine, raised BUN or blood creatinine, high blood potassium, reduced urine volume, generalised oedema with breathlessness or lassitude; rarely renal papillary necrosis, nephrotic syndrome, interstitial nephritis, peripheral oedema, acute pulmonary oedema, fluid retention, high blood pressure, heart failure or reduced fertility in women; occasionally swelling around the eye sockets; very rarely malaise, fever, nosebleed or worsening of inflammation.

Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious and possibly fatal cardiovascular thrombotic events, myocardial infarction and stroke, and serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulceration and perforation may occur.

People with uncontrolled high blood pressure, congestive heart failure, established ischaemic heart disease, peripheral arterial disease or cerebrovascular disease must avoid high-dose dexibuprofen (1,200 mg a day); people with cardiovascular risk factors such as high blood pressure, high blood lipids, diabetes or smoking who need high-dose ibuprofen must consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have or have had bronchial asthma; or if you have had asthma, urticaria or an allergic reaction to aspirin or another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic.

Do not take this medicine if you have gastrointestinal ulcer or signs of it, or have had it recur; if you have bleeding in the gastrointestinal tract, the cerebral blood vessels or elsewhere; if you have inflammatory bowel disease such as Crohn's disease or ulcerative colitis; or if you have had gastrointestinal bleeding or perforation caused by an earlier non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic.

Do not take this medicine if you have a severe blood disorder, liver impairment, kidney impairment, heart failure or high blood pressure; if you are being treated for pain occurring before or after coronary artery bypass surgery; or if you are 6 months or more pregnant.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have or have had a blood disorder, liver impairment or kidney impairment; if you have a blood clotting disorder or a tendency to bleed; if you have fluid retention or heart failure; if you have high blood pressure; if you have systemic lupus erythematosus or mixed connective tissue disease; if you have stomach cancer or alcoholism; if you have ischaemic heart disease, peripheral arterial disease, cerebrovascular disease or hepatic porphyria, or cardiovascular risk factors such as high blood pressure, high blood lipids, diabetes or smoking; or if you have had major surgery causing blood loss.

If you are breast-feeding, either stop taking this medicine or stop breast-feeding. Long-term use should be within 5 days. Dizziness or fatigue may occur; take care when driving or operating machinery.

While you are taking this medicine, do not take aspirin, another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic or high-dose methotrexate. Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are being given a corticosteroid, alcohol, digoxin, phenytoin, probenecid, sulfinpyrazone, a sulfonylurea, an ACE inhibitor or angiotensin II receptor antagonist, a diuretic, lithium, a coumarin anticoagulant (warfarin and the like), baclofen, an immunosuppressant (ciclosporin, tacrolimus, sirolimus), a thrombolytic, ticlopidine, an antithrombotic, a medicine that raises blood potassium (a potassium-sparing diuretic, an ACE inhibitor, an angiotensin II receptor antagonist, an immunosuppressant such as ciclosporin or tacrolimus, trimethoprim, heparin and the like), an inducer of CYP2C8 or CYP2C9 (rifampicin, phenobarbital), low-dose methotrexate (less than 15 mg a week), an antiplatelet medicine or a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor.

Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

groups.usage: To prevent motion sickness, take it 30 minutes to 1 hour before travelling: those aged 15 years and older take 1 tablet per dose; ages 11 years to under 15 years take 2/3 tablet per dose; ages 8 years to under 11 years take 1/2 tablet per dose. If a further dose is taken when symptoms appear, take the same amount again, leaving an interval of at least 4 hours, and take it no more than 3 times in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you are breast-feeding or if the user is a child aged 7 years or younger.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have had allergic symptoms caused by a medicine (rash, reddening of the skin, itching and the like); if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if you have glaucoma (eye pain, blurred vision and the like) or difficulty passing urine; or if you have a respiratory disease such as emphysema or chronic bronchitis.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, use it under the supervision of a guardian. Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery.

Do not take it together with another anti-emetic, a cold medicine, an antipyretic analgesic, an antihistamine, a sedative, an antitussive-expectorant or an alcoholic drink.

If rash, reddening of the skin, itching or palpitations occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Oral Suspension (101330ASS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for fever and pain caused by a cold, headache, neuralgia, muscle pain, menstrual pain, sprain pain, toothache, joint pain and rheumatic pain.
groups.usage: Ages 4 to 6 months: take 2.5 mL (80 mg) as 1 dose. Ages 7 to 23 months: take 3.5 mL (120 mg) as 1 dose. Ages 2 to 3 years: take 5 mL (160 mg) as 1 dose. Ages 4 to 6 years: take 7.5 mL (240 mg) as 1 dose. Ages 7 to 8 years: take 10 mL (320 mg) as 1 dose. Ages 9 to 10 years: take 12.5 mL (400 mg) as 1 dose. Age 11 years: take 15 mL (480 mg) as 1 dose. Age 12 years: take 20 mL (640 mg) as 1 dose. Take a dose every 4 to 6 hours when needed. If the body weight is known, dosing according to body weight is more appropriate. Take this medicine at the lowest effective dose for the shortest possible period, and do not take it more than 5 times in 1 day (75 mg/kg).
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

This medicine contains aspartame, which is metabolised in the body to phenylalanine. Do not take it if you have phenylketonuria and need to restrict your intake of phenylalanine.

Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported. If a skin rash or any other sign of hypersensitivity appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, a peptic ulcer, a severe blood disorder, liver impairment, kidney impairment, reduced cardiac function or a bleeding tendency, or if you have or have had aspirin asthma (an asthma attack triggered by a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory medicine).

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have or have had liver impairment, kidney impairment, a peptic ulcer, a blood disorder, a bleeding tendency, abnormal heart function or hypersensitivity; if you have bronchial asthma; if you are elderly; if the user is a child under 2 years of age; or if you are pregnant or breast-feeding.

Without the direction of a doctor or pharmacist, do not take it for pain for more than 10 days (adults) or more than 5 days (children), and do not take it for fever for more than 3 days.

Do not take it together with barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants, alcohol or another anti-inflammatory analgesic. Consult a pharmacist if you take it together with warfarin, lithium, a thiazide diuretic or flucloxacillin.

If signs of shock (difficulty breathing, flushing of the whole body, angioedema, urticaria and the like), an asthma attack, reduced platelets, granulocytopenia, haemolytic anaemia, methaemoglobinaemia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time), cyanosis, hypersensitivity (facial swelling, difficulty breathing, sweating, low blood pressure, shock), nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, gastrointestinal bleeding, peptic ulcer, perforation, rash, an allergic reaction, Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell syndrome), high anion gap metabolic acidosis, raised AST, raised ALT or fixed drug eruption occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Soft Capsule (E78400ACS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for constipation and for the relief of loss of appetite, abdominal bloating, abnormal fermentation in the bowel and haemorrhoid symptoms that accompany constipation.
groups.usage: Adults aged 15 years and over: take 1 to 2 capsules as 1 dose, 1 time in 1 day at bedtime. Take the smallest amount for the first dose, then increase or reduce the amount gradually while checking the shape and condition of the stool.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have an acute abdominal condition such as appendicitis, intestinal bleeding or ulcerative colitis; if you have intestinal obstruction; if you have or have had hypersensitivity to soya bean oil; or if you have hypersensitivity to soya beans or peanuts.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a child aged 10 years or under; if you are pregnant or may be pregnant; if you have severe abdominal pain, nausea or vomiting; if you are on a sodium-restricted diet; if you have had rectal bleeding or intestinal failure; if you have a disorder of fat metabolism such as hyperlipoproteinaemia, diabetic hyperlipidaemia or pancreatitis; if you are a patient in whom lipid emulsions must be given with care; if you are at risk from fat overload; or if you have or have had hypersensitivity to Food Yellow No. 5 (sunset yellow FCF) or Food Yellow No. 203 (quinoline yellow WS).

If your constipation does not improve after about 1 week of use, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist. Do not keep taking it for more than 1 week. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.

Do not take this medicine within 1 hour after taking an antacid or drinking milk. (Avoid drinking milk or taking an antacid within 1 hour after taking this medicine.)

If rash, reddening of the skin, itching, severe abdominal pain, diarrhoea, vomiting, abdominal discomfort or cramps occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.usage: Adults and those aged 12 years and over: take 1 tablet as 1 dose, 1 time in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if the user is a baby under 12 months of age; or if you have hypercalcaemia (an excess of calcium in the blood), sarcoidosis (an inflammatory disease of the whole body of unknown cause), kidney disease, kidney stones or severe renal failure.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if the user is a premature baby or an infant; if you have hyperoxaluria (excretion of an excessive amount of oxalate in the urine); if you have a gastrointestinal disease such as peptic ulcer, chronic ulcerative colitis or regional enteritis; if you have impaired heart or circulatory function, kidney impairment, low blood protein, gout or folate deficiency; or if you have or have had hypersensitivity to Food Yellow No. 4 or Food Yellow No. 5.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. This medicine may interfere with the detection of glucose in urine tests and may turn the urine yellow, which can affect laboratory test values. If your symptoms do not improve after about 1 month of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take it together with a phosphate, a calcium salt, an oral tetracycline, an antacid or levodopa. Consult a pharmacist if you take it together with a cardiac glycoside, an anti-aldosterone medicine or triamterene. Avoid tannin-containing drinks such as green tea and black tea while taking it and just before or after taking it.

If nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, loose stools, loss of appetite, abdominal bloating, constipation, low blood pressure, facial flushing, irregular heartbeat, skin rash, red spots, asystole (stopping of the heartbeat), depressed central nervous system function, dermatitis, a bad smell of the sweat or breath, hair loss, restlessness, gastrointestinal disorder, indigestion, upper abdominal pain or pulmonary oedema occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.
